features.name: Team Test client logs and GetLogHistoryAsync
features.summary: During a Team Test, LogService:GetLogHistoryAsync reads the recent logs of a collaborator's client or of the Team Test server. Collaborators' output also appears in the Output window, labeled with their name.
replaces: Asking collaborators to copy errors or send screenshots of their output
Reproducing a collaborator's bug yourself to see its output
features.guidance: During a Team Test the user starts, use execute_luau with datamodel_type Client to call LogService:GetLogHistoryAsync. Pass a collaborator's Player.User, or User.fromId(0) for the server, and wrap the call in pcall because it yields and can error. It returns message, messageType, and timestamp tables like GetLogHistory, and doesn't work in solo play or live games.

features.name: EditableMesh quad faces
features.summary: EditableMesh:AddFace(v1, v2, v3, v4) adds a quad (four-sided) face in one call, so you no longer build each quad from two triangles. Quads and triangles can be mixed on the same mesh. It works in Studio and in published experiences.
replaces: Two EditableMesh:AddTriangle calls per quad
EditableMesh:AddFace({v1, v2, v3, v4}) array signature
features.guidance: Build quads with EditableMesh:AddFace(v1, v2, v3, v4), passing the vertex IDs as separate arguments rather than an array, then set face data such as SetFaceNormals with four IDs. Pass three IDs to AddFace or use AddTriangle for triangles. Call EditableMesh:Triangulate if you need every quad split into two triangles. Each quad counts as two triangles toward the 20,000-triangle limit.

features.name: Wedge part collision geometry fix
features.summary: A fix for wrong wedge collision geometry began rolling out on 2026-11-09. Wedge flat edges no longer sink into box edges, and WorldRoot:GetPartsInPart no longer misses parts that overlap a wedge.
replaces: Workarounds for WorldRoot:GetPartsInPart missing parts that overlap wedges
features.guidance: Treat WorldRoot:GetPartsInPart results with wedges as accurate. Don't write workarounds for missed overlaps. Wedge glides and wedge flings no longer happen by themselves, so don't design obbies or movement code that depend on them. Emote corner clips and uplodges still work.

features.name: Device Simulator Network and Performance Simulators
features.summary: Studio's Device Simulator has a Network Simulator for latency, jitter, and packet loss, and a Performance Simulator that applies a device's typical graphics quality and RAM, so the user can test lower-end hardware during a playtest.
replaces: Stopping a playtest to switch the simulated device and then restarting it
Testing poor network conditions with a second device or a throttled router
Testing draw distance and streaming on physical lower-end devices
features.guidance: No MCP tool or API controls these simulators. When the user wants to test lag, packet loss, or low-end devices, ask them to open Test > Device Simulator and use the Network or Performance button. Memory simulation is off until they set Mode to Selected device or Manual, and only affects the client in Play, in places with Workspace.StreamingEnabled. Neither affects published experiences.

features.name: 500-stud minimum draw distance at low quality levels
features.summary: At the lowest graphics quality level, draw distance is now 500 studs instead of 200 on all platforms, and it rises faster at the next few levels. At low quality levels, terrain water stays transparent and Beam.Segments is no longer cut back as much.
replaces: Reading UserGameSettings.SavedQualityLevel to scale visual effects by hand
features.guidance: This applies to every game automatically, with nothing to turn on. Don't scale visual effects by reading UserGameSettings.SavedQualityLevel. Roblox plans to deprecate it, and it gets in the way of automatic scaling. Don't design around exact draw distances, and ask the user to check visuals at each level with Studio Settings > Rendering > Editor Quality Level.

features.name: Test teleports in Studio
features.summary: TeleportService:TeleportAsync now runs in Studio's Test and Team Test modes. The destination place opens as a new test server, so you can debug cross-place teleports without publishing.
replaces: Publishing every place and joining a live server to test teleports
Adding print statements and republishing to debug teleport flows
features.guidance: To test teleports, playtest in Studio's Test or Team Test mode, not Server & Clients. Studio MCP playtests work too. Only TeleportService:TeleportAsync works there, not Teleport, TeleportPartyAsync, or the other teleport methods. Save the destination place first, with save_place or by asking the user: a teleport loads its last saved version.

features.name: Prompt to Animation and Motion Rebuilder
features.summary: A Studio beta that makes R15 animation clips from a text prompt (Prompt to Animation) and converts R6 clips to R15 (Motion Rebuilder). Agents call the generate_animation MCP tool, and Assistant has /generate_animation.
replaces: Animating R15 clips by hand in the Animation Editor
Re-animating R6 clips by hand to move a game to R15
features.guidance: Ask the user to turn on Animation Generation in Assistant under File > Beta Features. Then call generate_animation with a prompt, and optionally a rig such as Workspace.Rig1, a length up to 10 seconds, or an R6 animation's asset ID to convert to R15. Converting a list of animations works, but it's rate limited.

features.name: UIShadow and per-corner UICorner radii
features.summary: UIShadow adds native drop shadows and glows to UI, with text, knockout and inset shadows and gradient fills. UICorner can now round each corner separately with TopLeftRadius, TopRightRadius, BottomLeftRadius and BottomRightRadius. Both work in published experiences.
replaces: Duplicating a TextLabel offset behind the original to fake a shadow
Image assets or 9-slice images for drop shadows and glows
Image assets or 9-slice workarounds for shapes with different corner radii
features.guidance: Add a UIShadow to the TextLabel or Frame instead of duplicating labels or using 9-slice shadow images, and toggle it with Enabled. Set Mode to Text for a shadow that follows the characters. For different corners, set the UDim properties TopLeftRadius, TopRightRadius, BottomLeftRadius and BottomRightRadius on one UICorner, because setting CornerRadius afterward overwrites all four.

features.name: CreateSurfaceAppearanceAsync with Asset IDs and Content
features.summary: AssetService:CreateSurfaceAppearanceAsync now accepts Asset IDs and DataModel Content as well as EditableImages, in any mix. Use it to build a SurfaceAppearance at runtime without first loading images into EditableImages.
replaces: Loading Asset ID images into EditableImages so they can be passed to CreateSurfaceAppearanceAsync
features.guidance: Ask the user to turn on "Mixed Content for CreateSurfaceAppearanceAsync" in File > Beta Features. It doesn't work in live experiences yet. Pass CreateSurfaceAppearanceAsync a table of maps such as ColorMap and MetalnessMap, using Content.fromUri("rbxassetid://...") for assets, and turn finished EditableImages into DataModel Content with CreateDataModelContentAsync(Content.fromObject(img)).

features.name: Content properties for asset references
features.summary: New *Content properties such as Sound.AudioContent and Animation.AnimationContent take a Content value and replace legacy string asset ID properties across many classes. Starting 2026-11-11, Studio saves asset references in the Content format.
replaces: Sound.SoundId
Animation.AnimationId
ParticleEmitter.Texture
FileMesh.MeshId
Sky.SkyboxBk
Legacy string-based asset ID properties (*Id or bare-name properties like Texture, Image, MouseIcon)
features.guidance: In new code, set asset properties through the *Content version (usually the legacy name with Content added, e.g. MeshId -> MeshContent, MouseIcon -> MouseIconContent) using a Content value, e.g. sound.AudioContent = Content.fromUri("rbxassetid://123"). Legacy names still work for reading and writing. Rojo users must update to v7.7.1 or later before 2026-11-11.

features.name: PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior on by default
features.summary: From November 11, 2026, Workspace.PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior set to Default acts like Enabled. The server destroys a Player 5 seconds after PlayerRemoving handlers run, and destroys an old Character right after CharacterRemoving handlers run, to prevent memory leaks.
replaces: Reading a Player's or Character's children after yielding in PlayerRemoving or CharacterRemoving
Re-parenting a removed Player or Character
Destroying removed Player and Character instances by hand to avoid memory leaks
features.guidance: From November 11, 2026, in PlayerRemoving and CharacterRemoving handlers, copy every value you need (UserId, leaderstats values, Character children) before any yield, then save the copies. Never re-parent a removed Player or Character. Disabled only works as a temporary opt-out until Phase 3 at the end of February, so write code that works with Enabled.

features.name: Open Cloud access from Studio MCP
features.summary: External MCP clients can call Open Cloud APIs through the Studio MCP server's open_cloud_invoke tool to manage developer products, game passes, settings, publishing, analytics, and asset uploads, within each game's MCP permissions. New Skills cover Open Cloud and asset import.
replaces: Setting up developer products and game passes, changing game settings, and reading analytics by hand in Creator Hub
Exporting, uploading, and fixing models from Blender or other 3D tools by hand
features.guidance: From an external MCP client, call Open Cloud with the open_cloud_invoke tool. No API key is needed. It only works for scopes the user turned on in Studio's MCP Permissions tab (Assistant > ... > Settings, or click MCP in Studio's bottom-right corner). Agents can't turn permissions on, so ask the user for any that are missing, and confirm before uploading because uploads are permanent.

features.name: Analytics Journeys (branching funnels)
features.summary: Journeys in Creator Analytics track players through stages that can branch and rejoin, shown as a Sankey chart with drop-off. Server scripts log progress with AnalyticsService:LogJourneyEvent(player, journeyName, nodeName).
replaces: Approximating branching player paths with several linear funnels
features.guidance: When players can take different paths, first publish a journey config through open_cloud_invoke, or ask the user to create it in Creator Hub under Analytics > Journeys. Then call AnalyticsService:LogJourneyEvent(player, journeyName, nodeName) from server code, after checking the player action is valid. Don't pass a stage number: Roblox works it out from the config.

features.name: Color3 contrast & luminance methods
features.summary: Color3 gains GetContrastingColor, GetContrastRatio, and GetLuminance for picking readable foreground colors on any background.
replaces: Hand-written WCAG contrast/luminance math
features.guidance: Use Color3:GetContrastingColor to choose readable text over dynamic backgrounds and GetContrastRatio to validate against WCAG thresholds instead of writing your own formulas.

features.name: DataModel.ServerLowMemoryWarning
features.summary: Server-side signal that fires when a live server moves into high memory usage, so scripts can free memory before an out-of-memory crash.
features.guidance: In server scripts, connect to game.ServerLowMemoryWarning to destroy debris/effects, unload unused map regions, and pause spawning until memory recovers.

features.name: Scene Generation
features.summary: Scene Generation is a Studio beta that turns a text prompt, reference images, or both into an editable scene of models, textures, and terrain for fast environment prototyping. Agents call the generate_scene MCP tool.
replaces: Pulling in and positioning hundreds of primitives by hand to block out a scene
Building many procedural models one at a time to fill an environment
features.guidance: To block out an environment, call generate_scene with a textPrompt, reference images, or both, and optionally a bounding box position and size. Say what to create and what not to, such as "don't generate any terrain". Generated procedural models have attributes, so change those instead of rebuilding the models.

features.name: Team Test Server Inspection
features.summary: Server Inspection is a Studio beta that adds a read-only Server view during Team Test. It shows the live server's DataModel, properties, and 3D world, including ServerScriptService and ServerStorage, and supports breakpoints in server scripts.
features.guidance: Only the user can turn it on and use it. When server state needs checking during Team Test, ask them to enable File > Beta Features > Server Inspection, open a Team Create place, start Team Test from the ribbon, and switch to the Server view. Edits in the Server view never reach the server, so changes still go in Edit.

features.name: Orthographic Camera
features.summary: Camera.ProjectionType can be set to Orthographic so objects keep the same size at any distance, for 2D, isometric, and top-down games.
replaces: Shrinking Camera.FieldOfView to ~1 degree and moving the camera far away to fake orthographic projection
features.guidance: Studio beta: ask the user to turn it on in File > Beta Features. It works only in Studio, and published games can't use them yet. Set Camera.ProjectionType to Orthographic rather than faking it with a tiny FieldOfView, and zoom with OrthographicSize instead of moving the camera.

features.name: Web Play (play Roblox games in a browser)
features.summary: Web Play beta lets creators test their own games in Chrome on macOS, Windows, and Android before it opens to all players. Games run on WebGL with extra browser memory and performance overhead, and games should enable Workspace.ImprovedPhysicsReplication.
features.guidance: Creator beta: only the owner, or a group game's editors and testers, can play it in Chrome from Creator Hub, so ask the user to test there. Turn on Workspace.ImprovedPhysicsReplication, keep memory and performance in check for the browser, and don't count on high-quality shaders, advanced lighting, voice chat, or video playback on the web.

features.name: Prompt-to-Avatar game character generation
features.summary: Prompt-to-Avatar turns a text prompt into a 2D concept and then an R15 or Advanced R15 game character model, with static or dynamic heads. Agents call the generate_avatar MCP tool, and it's also in Avatar Setup and Assistant.
replaces: Building each game character model from scratch by hand
features.guidance: Ask the user to turn on Prompt-to-Avatar in File > Beta Features, then call generate_avatar. It's for game characters: bodies with built-in clothing can't be published as avatar bodies, so use the modesty pipeline for those. Write prompts as: style anchor, full body, proportions, character, outfit top to bottom, 2-3 colors plus an accent.

features.name: Radial, conic, and elliptical UIGradients
features.summary: UIGradient gains Type (Enum.GradientType.Linear, Radial, Conical, or Elliptical), TileMode, and Scale.
replaces: Radial-gradient images or stacked UIGradients to fake radial/conic fills
features.guidance: For radial, conic, or elliptical fills, set UIGradient.Type to Enum.GradientType.Radial, Conical, or Elliptical instead of using images.

features.name: Input Action System + Input Action Manager
features.summary: Cross-platform input framework (InputContext/InputAction/InputBinding) with ResponseCurve, modifier chords, touch keycodes, UIModifier, ClampMagnitudeToOne and Vector3Scale, plus the Input Action Manager editor. Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem opts into IAS player scripts.
replaces: ContextActionService:BindAction
UserInputService.InputBegan for gameplay actions
Hand-written key-combination checks for shortcuts
Hand-written normalization of diagonal movement input
Legacy default player scripts and PlayerModule internals such as GetControls()
features.guidance: Build controls with InputContext/InputAction/InputBinding via execute_luau, not ContextActionService or UserInputService. Set Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem to Enabled and avoid PlayerModule GetControls(). To audit bindings and conflicts, suggest the Input Action Manager under Windows > Input > Actions. No MCP tool runs it, and its instances work in live games.

features.name: Shapecast margins, size gradients, and overrides
features.summary: Blockcast, Spherecast, and Shapecast run on a faster, more accurate implementation and gain margins, size gradients, and CFrame/size overrides.
replaces: Moving or resizing a part just to shapecast it from another position or size
features.guidance: Use RaycastParams.Margin to round/inflate cast shapes and the cframe/size overrides on WorldRoot:Shapecast instead of temporarily moving parts.

features.name: TeleportOptions server ID targeting
features.summary: TeleportOptions gains ReservedServerId and VipServerId (GUID strings) so TeleportAsync can explicitly target reserved and VIP servers.
replaces: Relying on inferred VIP-server destination behavior during teleports
features.guidance: To keep players in a private server across teleports, set TeleportOptions.ReservedServerId or VipServerId to the target server's game.PrivateServerId.

features.name: Plugin window screenshots in Studio
features.summary: Studio can copy a single window, such as Output, a viewport, or a third-party plugin, to the clipboard with Ctrl+Shift+2 or the Screenshot Plugin action, without the rest of Studio.
replaces: Full-screen or OS screenshots cropped by hand to show one Studio window
features.guidance: No MCP tool triggers it. Read Output with get_console_output and see the viewport with screen_capture. For any other window, such as a plugin's, ask the user to press Ctrl+Shift+2 (rebindable in Configure Shortcuts) or run Screenshot Plugin from quick actions, select the window, and paste the image into the conversation.

features.name: Device Trust API
features.summary: Check whether a player's device reports OS or Roblox app modifications, to gate features or block bots and modified clients. Only Android is supported so far; unsupported platforms report Unknown.
features.guidance: Read device trust on the server, through the IntegrityService.EvaluatePlayerDeviceTrust callback or Player.DeviceTrustLevel, never on the client, which can spoof it. Use it to gate trading, chat, or competitive matchmaking, and handle Unknown for unsupported platforms.

features.name: AnimatedImages (2D flipbook animation)
features.summary: Early Access: import Aseprite (.ase) files and play flipbook animation tracks on ImageLabels at runtime via AnimatedImageService and AnimationPlayer.
replaces: Manually stepping ImageLabel.ImageRectOffset/ImageRectSize for sprite-sheet animation
features.guidance: Early Access and Studio-only, so published places can't use it yet. Only use it if the user is enrolled; otherwise fall back to sprite sheets. Read and set the clip and frame with AnimationPlayer:GetParameter() and SetParameter(), which replaced the Track and CurrentFrame properties.

features.name: UGC Validation Visualization
features.summary: UGC Validation Visualization, on Studio's Avatar tab, runs Marketplace validation on bodies, heads, layered clothing, and rigid accessories, marks errors and warnings on the asset, and reports Asset Quality before publishing.
replaces: Uploading to the Marketplace to find out which UGC validation checks fail
features.guidance: No MCP tool or Engine API runs it. Before the user publishes a UGC body, head, layered clothing item, or rigid accessory, ask them to open Avatar > UGC Validation Visualization, select the asset in Explorer, click Run Validation, and pick the asset type. Errors show in red and warnings, such as Asset Quality, in yellow; ask them to share the messages so you can help fix them.

features.name: Custom Terrain Materials (Expanded Terrain)
features.summary: The Expanded Terrain setting on Workspace enables up to 62 custom terrain materials, configured in code with Terrain:SetMaterialSlot, plus terrain storage and streaming improvements that make place files smaller and load faster. Games that use them can be published and played by everyone.
features.guidance: Ask the user to set Workspace's Expanded Terrain property to Enabled, then save, close, and reopen the place; Early Access places need this too. Then call Terrain:SetMaterialSlot(slot 2-63, baseMaterial, variantName or "", color) and write slot numbers with the SolidMaterialIndex channel of Terrain:WriteVoxelChannels. Custom materials work in published games; performance gains apply only in Studio for now.

features.name: Text-to-speech asset creation
features.summary: AssetService:CreateAssetAsync accepts AudioTextToSpeech objects with Enum.AssetType.Audio to bake speech assets in Studio.
replaces: Running text-to-speech at play time for fixed voice lines
features.guidance: Studio Beta. For static voice lines, generate assets in Studio with CreateAssetAsync instead of synthesizing at play time to avoid rate limits and latency.

features.name: TextChatService platform-integrated chat
features.summary: Chat is moving to native systems (TextChatCommands, TextChannelWindow, Quick Words); message content will no longer be accessible in code. Migration required by May 2027.
replaces: Custom chat UIs/features that read message content in code
features.guidance: Don't build new features that read chat message text; use TextChatCommand and native chat UI. To test, ask the user to set TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat to Enabled in the Properties window, because scripts can't set it.

features.name: In-game EditableImage publishing
features.summary: AssetService:PromptCreateAssetAsync is renamed to PromptCreatePlatformContentAsync, takes an Object, and can publish EditableImages to the player's inventory.
replaces: AssetService:PromptCreateAssetAsync
features.guidance: Use AssetService:PromptCreatePlatformContentAsync (not PromptCreateAssetAsync) for in-game creation prompts, including EditableImage uploads. Call it from a server script. In Studio it only works in a published place, and the game needs Allow Mesh / Image APIs turned on.

features.name: In-Experience Creation: Makeup, Accessories, Clothing
features.summary: Players can create, buy, and save makeup, accessories, and layered clothing to their inventory from inside a game. PromptCreateMakeupAsync combines makeup layers, and PromptCreateAvatarAssetAsync saves one accessory or clothing item (accessories and clothing are a client beta).
features.guidance: Makeup: cache projection data with WrapTextureTransfer:PrepareProjectionMeshDataAsync, make decals with AssetService:CreateDecalAsync, then call PromptCreateMakeupAsync. Accessories and layered clothing (client beta, works in published games): check with ValidateUGCAccessoryAsync, then call PromptCreateAvatarAssetAsync with the user's token ID. Await the ModerationCompleted events before use.

features.name: Package Overrides
features.summary: Package Overrides lets you edit a package copy in your place and still get updates from the source package. Studio records each edit as an override and reapplies it after every update.
replaces: Breaking a package's link to customize one copy
Leaving an edited package on an old version to keep local changes
features.guidance: Studio beta: ask the user to update to Studio 743 or later, turn on Package Overrides in File > Beta Features, and restart Studio. To customize one copy of a package, edit it in place and keep the link: don't break the link or pin an old version. Edits win over source changes to the same property, and Auto-Update can stay on.

features.name: Early testers and guided publishing flow
features.summary: Creators can invite up to 10 friends or Group members as early testers from Studio's Collaborate dialog. A guided publishing flow, synced between Studio and Creator Hub, lets games with no age-restricted content reach players 16 and older by answering one question.
replaces: Private and Limited audience settings (now the Playtest publish option)
Completing the full Maturity and Compliance Questionnaire to publish to 16+ audiences
Meeting full Kids and Select publishing requirements to gather early feedback
features.guidance: Adding early testers is up to the user. When they want friends to preview an unpublished game, tell them to click Collaborate in Studio, open the Early testers tab, and add up to 10 friends (or Group members for Group-owned games), or use Creator Hub > Configure > Permissions. When publishing, they choose Playtest or Public; Playtest replaces Private and Limited.

features.name: SLIM debug tints
features.summary: SLIM debug tints color models by streaming state, level of detail, or transcoding status, to check that SLIM is active and models are optimized before publishing.
features.guidance: Only the user can turn these on. When checking SLIM, ask them to enable File > Beta Features > SLIM Debug Tints and pick a SLIM Tint Mode from the viewport's Visualization Modes menu, or in Roblox Player pick SlimTintMode in the Developer Console's DebugVisualizations menu (needs Edit permission). Transcoding status is Studio only; data model state and LoD also work in Play mode and Player.

features.name: Animation Graph State Machines and Expressions
features.summary: The Animation Graph Editor adds State Machine nodes, which hold states and the transitions between them, and Luau Expression nodes for parameter math. Animation transitions and blend math can now live in the graph instead of in a script.
replaces: Tracking animation state in a Luau script and passing it to a Select node
Computing blend weights and other derived graph values in a script before passing them in with AnimationTrack:SetParameter
features.guidance: Studio beta: ask the user to turn on Animation Graphs State Machines in File > Beta Features. It works only in Studio, so published experiences can't use it yet. Put state transitions in a State Machine node and parameter math in Expression nodes, and keep scripts for setting gameplay values with AnimationTrack:SetParameter.

features.name: Text-to-speech automatic translation
features.summary: AudioTextToSpeech.AutoLocalize (default true) speaks generated speech in each player's language, for 11 languages.
replaces: Translating TTS text manually per locale
features.guidance: Use AudioTextToSpeech with AutoLocalize enabled instead of translating TTS strings yourself.

features.name: if local and while local bindings
features.summary: Luau beta syntax that declares a variable in an if, elseif, or while condition: `if local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") then`, or `while local job = table.remove(jobs) do`.
replaces: Declaring a local and then checking it on the next line
while true loops that break when a fetched value is nil
features.guidance: Studio beta: ask the user to turn on If Local/Const Bindings in File > Beta Features. Where it's on, prefer `if local x = expr then` for find-and-check code and `while local x = expr do` for loops that run until a value is nil. Each binding takes one name and one value.

features.name: Collision summaries API
features.summary: BasePart:BindToCollisionSummaries subscribes to precise collision data: contact points, normals, and relative velocities.
replaces: Touched plus AssemblyLinearVelocity guesses for impact strength
features.guidance: Use BindToCollisionSummaries when you need impact strength, contact points or normals, not Touched.

features.name: Frustum streaming
features.summary: Player.FrustumStreaming streams in distant instances inside the player's camera view, such as scoped targets or the road ahead.
replaces: Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync to fake view-based streaming
features.guidance: Enable Player.FrustumStreaming for view-dependent streaming instead of repeatedly calling RequestStreamAroundAsync at a look point.

features.name: Texture generation Quality mode and mesh segmentation
features.summary: Retexture a mesh in Fast (1K color) or beta Quality (4K PBR) mode, split imported meshes into named parts, and in beta generate models already split into parts. Use the generate_texture, segment_mesh, generate_mesh and generate_procedural_model tools, or GenerationService:GenerateModelAsync in-game.
replaces: Segmenting only generated meshes (imported meshes can now be segmented too)
Color-only 1K generated textures when roughness and metalness maps are needed
Generating a single-mesh model and splitting it into parts by hand
features.guidance: Call generate_texture with a textPrompt and instance_path (Fast to iterate, Quality beta for 4K PBR maps). segment_mesh splits an imported mesh into up to five named parts, and generate_mesh and generate_procedural_model return up to 8 parts if the user has Segment by parts on in File > Beta Features. In game code, pass part names as SchemaDefinition.Groups to GenerationService:GenerateModelAsync.

features.name: Tunable collision fidelity
features.summary: MeshPart.CollisionFidelity gains Tunable, with MeshPart.CollisionPrecision to trade performance for precision per mesh.
replaces: Choosing only between Box/Hull/Default/PreciseConvexDecomposition
features.guidance: Set CollisionFidelity to Tunable and adjust CollisionPrecision when Default is too coarse but PreciseConvexDecomposition is too expensive.

features.name: PlayerFeedback API and Player Support reporting
features.summary: SocialService:PromptFeedbackSubmissionAsync opens a Roblox-designed dialog where players type feedback about your experience. The feedback shows up in Creator Hub under Audience > Feedback and is summarized in Creator Analytics Insights.
replaces: Custom in-game feedback and bug report forms
Collecting bug reports through community posts, DMs, or off-platform servers
features.guidance: Instead of building a custom feedback form, call SocialService:PromptFeedbackSubmissionAsync inside task.spawn, since it yields. Call it after a milestone like a level, round win, or tutorial, not during the core loop. Passing FeedbackType = Enum.FeedbackType.PlayerSupport for issue reports is still early access through a Roblox survey sign-up, and those reports go to Audience > Player Support.

features.name: Roblox-native Friends and Global Leaderboards
features.summary: Roblox can show persistent Friends and Global leaderboard tabs in its in-game leaderboard UI. It reads them from an OrderedDataStore you register in Creator Hub, so you don't need your own backend or UI for these views.
replaces: Custom-built friends and global leaderboard backends for the in-game leaderboard UI
features.guidance: To get persistent Friends and Global tabs, keep scores in an OrderedDataStore keyed by user ID with numeric values. Register it in Creator Hub and turn on 'Active leaderboard'. Your scripts still write scores for every player, not just the top 100, and should give each player a default score when they join. Custom leaderboards built with OrderedDataStore:GetSortedAsync can still be used alongside it.

features.name: EditableMesh batching and vertex-face APIs
features.summary: EditableMesh gains Batch* methods (BatchSetValues, BatchAdd, BatchGetVertexAttributes, ...) and parallel queries for fast bulk edits, plus vertex-face getters/setters (SetVertexFaceColor), GetVertexFaces/Colors, GetFacesWithColor-style lookups, and cloning via CreateEditableMeshAsync.
replaces: Per-vertex loops of SetPosition/SetColor/AddVertex for bulk edits
EditableMesh:GetFacesWithAttribute
EditableMesh:GetVerticesWithAttribute
Looping GetFaceVertices/GetFaceColors/SetFaceColors to change one face corner
features.guidance: Use Batch* methods for bulk EditableMesh edits instead of per-element setters in a loop. To change a face corner, loop GetVertexFaces(vid) and call SetVertexFaceColor/Normal/UV(vid, fid, ...); look up IDs with GetFacesWith*/GetVerticesWith* (Color, Normal, UV) instead of deprecated Get*WithAttribute. Clone with AssetService:CreateEditableMeshAsync(Content.fromObject(mesh)).

features.name: Character Controller Library Custom Abilities
features.summary: The Character Controller Library (AvatarAbilities) adds Sprint and Crouch as default abilities. Its Custom Abilities API lets you define abilities as modules and add them at runtime with getAbilityManager(character) and AbilityManager:AddAbility, or build on the default ones with extendAbility.
replaces: AvatarAbilities.addAbilityForCharacter
AvatarAbilities.removeAbilityForCharacter
Direct ability helper methods on CharacterController
ExtendAbility, PolledSensor, ReactiveSensor, ThrottledSensor (renamed to camelCase)
Hand-written sprint and crouch scripts
features.guidance: Studio Beta: build abilities as modules with OnSetup/OnStart/OnStop/OnUpdate/OnTeardown and add them via AvatarAbilities.getAbilityManager(character) or waitForAbilityManager(character):AddAbility(...). Use camelCase static functions (extendAbility, polledSensor), put button behavior in Input.Mode rather than RunsWhile, and use Server Authority with Workspace.SignalBehavior set to Deferred.

features.name: Auto-Reimport
features.summary: Studio's Auto-Reimport watches the source file behind a Model, SurfaceAppearance, or Decal and reimports the instance whenever that file changes on disk, so you don't have to reimport by hand.
replaces: Manually running Reimport in Studio after every change to an external source file
features.guidance: Studio beta that the user sets up: they turn on Auto-Reimport in File > Beta Features, then right-click an instance with saved Reimport settings in the Explorer and select Reimport > Auto-Reimport. After that, changes to its source file on disk reimport on their own. The setting lasts only for the session, so it has to be turned on again after Studio restarts.

features.name: Collision groups on WorldRoot (PhysicsService deprecated)
features.summary: Collision group management moved from PhysicsService to WorldRoot (Workspace and WorldModels). The PhysicsService collision group methods are deprecated.
replaces: PhysicsService:RegisterCollisionGroup
PhysicsService:CollisionGroupSetCollidable
PhysicsService:CollisionGroupsAreCollidable
features.guidance: Call RegisterCollisionGroup / CollisionGroupSetCollidable on workspace (a WorldRoot), not PhysicsService.

features.name: Enhanced Freecam (roll, FOV, player lock, effects)
features.summary: Freecam, now on the Input Action System through Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, adds camera roll, speed and stiffness tuning, player lock, UI hiding, and custom post-processing for cinematic shots in Studio and live experiences.
replaces: Hand-written free-fly camera scripts for capturing trailers, cinematics, and screenshots
features.guidance: To get the enhanced Freecam controls, enable Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem. Toggle Freecam with LeftShift + P in Studio Play/Test and in live clients. Open the config menu with the Up arrow or D-pad Up. In live experiences, only the place owner, users with edit permissions, or users the experience's code grants camera permissions can use it.

features.name: Publish with Notes (auto-generated publish notes)
features.summary: Studio's Version History can draft publish notes by summarizing the version notes saved since the last publish, so teams get a record of what went live without writing it up by hand.
replaces: Writing a summary of each publish by hand from the team's version notes
features.guidance: The user drafts and approves these in Studio. When they publish, suggest File > Publish with Notes, or Window > Version History > Edit Notes for a version already published. The draft only uses version notes saved since the last publish, so suggest short version notes along the way. Nothing is saved until the user approves the draft.

features.name: Asset Manager folders, search, and bulk actions
features.summary: The revamped Studio Asset Manager is fully released. It sorts assets into folders, searches inventories by asset ID and date, shares many assets at once or makes them Open Use, manages Model and Package versions, and inserts several assets at once by drag-and-drop.
replaces: Legacy Asset Manager workflows that organize assets only by type
Sharing assets one at a time on the Creator Hub
Inserting animation assets only as KeyframeSequences
Dragging assets into the workspace one at a time
Creating new asset aliases
features.guidance: Find and insert assets with the search_asset and insert_asset MCP tools. No MCP tool drives the Asset Manager, so point users to Home > Assets for folders, search (asset IDs, created_after=), Share or Make Open Use, version history, multi-select drag-and-drop insert, and right-click copying of asset IDs. New aliases can't be created, so reference assets by ID. Existing aliases still work.

features.name: Assemble and publish avatar looks in Studio
features.summary: Studio's Avatar > Setup tool assembles avatar looks and publishes them for management in the Creator Dashboard. It replaces the Universal App avatar publishing flow, which is deprecated on October 21, 2026.
replaces: Universal App avatar publishing flow
features.guidance: Assembling and publishing a look is up to the user. Tell them to open Avatar > Setup in Studio, add items with Add AssetID, and save with Create Avatar Look. The look needs at least one 3D item uploaded by the user, or by the group it publishes for, or it can't be published. Point them here instead of the Universal App flow, deprecated on October 21, 2026.

features.name: Studio MCP studio_id routing
features.summary: Every Studio MCP Server tool call now takes a studio_id that names the target Studio, which makes multi-Studio, multi-agent workflows reliable. set_active_studio is removed. list_roblox_studios now also returns each Studio's Place ID.
replaces: set_active_studio MCP tool
Relying on session state to pick which Studio an MCP tool call targets
features.guidance: Call list_roblox_studios first, then pass that Studio's studio_id on every Studio MCP tool call. Never call set_active_studio, which has been removed. If two open Studios share a name, use the Place ID from list_roblox_studios to pick the right one. Local places have no Place ID and are listed by name only.

features.name: IsVerified verification levels
features.summary: Player:IsVerified now takes an optional Enum.VerifiedLevel (Low or High) so you can require a stronger verification threshold.
features.guidance: Player:IsVerified() defaults to Enum.VerifiedLevel.Low, which suits features like trading. Pass Enum.VerifiedLevel.High for high-stakes features such as ranked matchmaking.

features.name: Collections (CollectionService:CreateCollection)
features.summary: CollectionService:CreateCollection(query, root) returns a Collection, a group of instances defined by a live query. Instances join and leave as they match, and callbacks like OnAdded, OnRemoved and On{Event} connect and disconnect for you.
replaces: CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal and CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal with manual per-instance connection tracking
CollectionService:GetTagged loops that connect events to each tagged instance
Watching property or attribute changes by hand to decide when an instance enters or leaves a group
features.guidance: Use CollectionService:CreateCollection("Selector") and assign callbacks such as function c.OnAdded(inst), c.OnRemoved, c.OnTouched or c.OnHeartbeat(inst, dt), instead of wiring tag signals and tracking connections yourself. Queries use QueryDescendants selector syntax, and [$Attr = value] matches attributes. ForEach and RunService callbacks can't yield.

features.name: InputActionLabel
features.summary: InputActionLabel is a UI instance that automatically displays an InputAction's current binding (key or gamepad button) using the new InputAction.PreferredBinding property.
replaces: Hand-written UserInputService.LastInputTypeChanged logic to swap keyboard/gamepad hint images
features.guidance: Studio Beta. To show on-screen hotkey hints for an InputAction, use InputActionLabel instead of manually swapping images per input type.

features.name: Animation Clip Editor import: glTF, clips, settings
features.summary: The Animation Clip Editor importer takes FBX and glTF files and now has Rig Scale, Rest Pose Source, Rig Type (R15 or Custom) and track selection settings. Animations on models brought in with the Universal Importer are saved to AnimSaves automatically.
replaces: The old FBX-only Animation Clip Editor importer
Converting glTF animations to FBX before importing them into the Animation Editor
Splitting multi-clip animation files into one file per clip
Importing a model's animation separately in the Animation Clip Editor after importing the model
Rescaling imported animations by hand to match studs
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs these importers. Ask the user to click From File in the Animation Editor and set Rig Scale, Rig Type (R15 or Custom), Rest Pose Source and track, or to import the animated model with the Universal Importer. Then find the clips with search_game_tree using the keyword AnimSaves. They're saved only locally, so ask the user to upload them.

features.name: Server Management, server history and restarts
features.summary: Open Cloud game server APIs, starting with GameServers_ListGameServers, list an experience's servers with their stats and restart servers by place version. ListGameServers now also returns servers terminated in the last 30 days, with status, terminationTime and uptime fields.
replaces: All-or-nothing restarts of every server or of all outdated servers
Leaving Creator Hub to find details about individual running servers
Having no record of why a server shut down once it left the active server list
features.guidance: Call GameServers_ListGameServers and other Open Cloud game server APIs with open_cloud_invoke to list servers or restart them by place version. To diagnose crashes, filter by server_status and read each server's status, terminationTime and uptime (kept 30 days). They need Read (list) or Edit (restart) permission and have a low rate limit: admin tools only, not matchmaking or server browsers.

features.name: Predictive Streaming
features.summary: Predictive Streaming is an opt-in Instance Streaming feature that loads areas a player will probably need soon. It does this by prefetching likely spawn points when the player dies and keeping a CFrame origin streamed in. Turn it on by setting Workspace.PredictiveStreamingMode to Enabled.
replaces: Hand-written Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync prefetches at spawn locations before respawn
Hand-written Player:AddReplicationFocus foci to keep a CFrame origin streamed in
features.guidance: In games with Workspace.StreamingEnabled set to true, use execute_luau in Edit to set workspace.PredictiveStreamingMode = Enum.PredictiveStreamingMode.Enabled, then call save_place. It needs no code changes. Keep using Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync or Player:AddReplicationFocus where you need precise control. Predictive Streaming works alongside them and won't add a second focus where one already exists.

features.name: Restart notifications (ServerRestartScheduled)
features.summary: DataModel.ServerRestartScheduled fires before a scheduled server restart, for developer restarts (Enum.CloseReason.DeveloperUpdate) and now Roblox maintenance (Enum.CloseReason.RobloxMaintenance). It passes the restart time, source and attributes so code can save progress or teleport players.
features.guidance: In a server Script, connect game.ServerRestartScheduled:Connect(function(restartTime, source, attributes)) and branch on source: Enum.CloseReason.RobloxMaintenance (attributes empty, restart usually 30+ min away) or Enum.CloseReason.DeveloperUpdate. Warn clients, save data and call TeleportService:TeleportAsync(game.PlaceId, players) at a convenient moment, with error handling.

features.name: Instance attributes and InstanceHandle
features.summary: Attributes can now point at another Instance directly. Pass an Instance to Instance:SetAttribute, and Instance:GetAttribute returns an InstanceHandle that you resolve with Get() or Wait(). This replaces ObjectValue children and works in published experiences.
replaces: ObjectValue children used to hold a reference to another Instance
Sending raw Instance references over RemoteEvents when the Instance may not have replicated to the client yet
features.guidance: Store references with part:SetAttribute("Target", instance) instead of adding an ObjectValue child. GetAttribute returns an InstanceHandle, not an Instance, so call handle:Get() (no yield, nil if not available locally) or handle:Wait(timeout) before using it. To send an Instance the client may not have yet, fire InstanceHandle.new(instance) through a RemoteEvent.

features.name: Animation Graph
features.summary: Animation Graphs are out of beta. You build node graphs that blend, select, mask and sequence clips in Studio's Animation Graph Editor, and they now play and replicate in published experiences. Scripts drive graph parameters with AnimationTrack:SetParameter.
replaces: Hand-written Luau that blends and switches between many AnimationTracks for locomotion and combat transitions
features.guidance: No MCP tool creates graphs, so ask the user to build one in the Animation Graph Editor (Avatar tab) and add its parameters. Load a graph with Animator:LoadAnimation the same way as a clip, then update it with track:SetParameter("Speed", value), using the graph's parameter names. Graphs now play in published experiences and replicate automatically, so you don't need clip-based fallbacks.

features.name: Data Stores experience-level limits and Extended Services
features.summary: In-game and Open Cloud Data Stores requests now share one per-experience budget for each request type: 300 + CCU x multiplier per minute. Storage is 500 MB + 1 MB per lifetime player. DataStoreService:SetRateLimitForRequestType raises per-server limits.
replaces: Retrying throttled DataStore calls immediately or at a fixed interval
Treating per-server request limits as the only DataStore access limit
Separate request limits for Open Cloud and in-game Data Stores
features.guidance: Wrap DataStore calls in pcall and retry GameServerThrottled and ExperienceThrottled errors with exponential backoff and jitter. Open Cloud calls, including open_cloud_invoke, share that budget, so throttle them; raise server limits with DataStoreService:SetRateLimitForRequestType. Ask the user to check usage in the Creator Dashboard or sign up for Extended Services; no MCP tool does either.

features.name: ClipsDescendants clipping for rotated UI and Path2D
features.summary: A parent GuiObject's ClipsDescendants now clips rotated children and Path2D instances, so nested CanvasGroups and custom math aren't needed. It's on by default as of Sept 24, 2026. StarterGui.ClipsDescendantsSupportsRotation is removed in November 2026.
replaces: Nested CanvasGroups to clip rotated UI elements
Custom math to clip rotated shapes or Path2D curves
features.guidance: To clip rotated GuiObjects and Path2D, set ClipsDescendants on the parent. Don't use CanvasGroup or math workarounds. To keep an element unclipped, set the parent's ClipsDescendants to false or make the element a higher-ZIndex sibling. Leave StarterGui.ClipsDescendantsSupportsRotation Enabled and don't reference it in code: it's removed in November 2026.

features.name: Creator-authored Assistant Skills
features.summary: Creators can now write their own Assistant Skills, which are Markdown guides for their conventions and workflows. Skills also reach third-party MCP clients through the Studio MCP server. A new Roblox-authored unit-test Skill writes, runs, and debugs Luau tests for ModuleScripts.
replaces: Re-explaining coding conventions or team workflows in every conversation
features.guidance: Before you build, call the skill MCP tool to load the user's Skills and follow them, such as their naming and module-structure rules. Use the unit-test Skill to add tests to ModuleScripts. No MCP tool creates or edits Skills, so ask the user to do it in the Skills tab of Assistant Settings or with /rbx-create-skill.

features.name: Server Authority and BindToSimulation
features.summary: Server Authority is fully released. Set Workspace.AuthorityMode to Server to make the server authoritative, with client prediction and rollback in RunService:BindToSimulation. Camera InputAction no longer replicates, so use Player:GetCameraState() instead.
replaces: FixedHeartbeat (Early Access Server Authority callback)
Framerate-dependent gameplay logic in RunService.PreSimulation or RunService.Heartbeat
Hand-written server-side anti-cheat checks for client-controlled physics
Keeping AnimationTrack references across frames
Creating and removing a StringValue to trigger tool slash or lunge animations
The old LocalScript Animate script that keeps state in local variables
Waiting for server confirmation before showing client-spawned instances such as projectiles
Camera replication through Player.InputContexts.CameraContext.CameraAction
features.guidance: Run gameplay in RunService:BindToSimulation, with state in attributes; Instance.new there is predicted. Use execute_luau to set Workspace.AuthorityMode to Server, SignalBehavior to Deferred, and turn on NextGenerationReplication, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, StreamingEnabled and UseFixedSimulation. Read a player's camera with Player:GetCameraState(), not CameraContext.CameraAction.

features.name: GuiButton.SecondaryActivated
features.summary: GuiButton.SecondaryActivated is a new event that fires for secondary input on any GuiButton: right-click, a touch long press over 1000 ms, R3 on a controller, and Alt+Enter during keyboard navigation. One handler covers context menus and secondary actions on every device.
replaces: Separate per-device handlers for right-click and long-press on GUI buttons
Using GuiButton.MouseButton2Click alone for secondary button actions
features.guidance: For context menus, secondary actions or long-press behavior on a GuiButton, connect button.SecondaryActivated in a LocalScript instead of writing separate handlers for mouse, touch and gamepad. Keep GuiButton.Activated for the main action. Use script_grep to find MouseButton2Click handlers on buttons and move them over with multi_edit.

features.name: LibMP MicroProfiler API and automated profiling
features.summary: Assistant and Studio MCP agents can now analyze a paused MicroProfiler capture or a binary dump with LibMP, the MicroProfiler Luau API. They find bottlenecks and propose fixes. Scripts can also use LibMP to read MicroProfiler data in Studio and in live games.
replaces: Reading performance data by hand in the MicroProfiler UI
Pressing Dump in the MicroProfiler at the right moment to capture a snapshot
Exporting MicroProfiler captures to text or JSON to feed to an LLM
features.guidance: Ask the user to open the MicroProfiler (Ctrl+F6) and pause on a frame spike (Ctrl+P), or to save Dump > Dump in binary format, then analyze it with LibMP per github.com/Roblox/libmp/releases/download/latest/SKILL.md. Loop: reproduce with start_stop_play, profile, fix with multi_edit, retest. For in-game profiling, ask the user to add the LibMP module from github.com/Roblox/libmp.

features.name: Next-Gen Draggers (Move, Rotate, Scale)
features.summary: A Studio beta that updates the built-in Move, Rotate, and Scale tools. It adds planar and view-space dragging, trackball rotation, snapping ticks on the active axis, and new Dragger Visualization settings. It adds no Engine API or MCP tool.
replaces: Repeated single-axis drags to place parts across two axes
Rotating one axis at a time to get a free-form orientation
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs the draggers. When the user is moving parts by hand, suggest they turn on Next-Gen Draggers in File > Beta Features and restart Studio, then adjust it under File > Studio Settings > Selection > Dragger Visualization. It only changes Studio's built-in tools, not published experiences, plugins, or scripts, so keep placing instances with execute_luau.

features.name: Game Server Logs (ListGameServerLogs)
features.summary: Error and warning logs from each live game server are now available through the Open Cloud ListGameServerLogs API and a Logs tab on the Creator Hub Server Details page. Use them to find out what went wrong on a specific server.
replaces: Writing custom error loggers that send server errors to external services over HttpService
Using only the aggregated Error Report to debug a specific server
features.guidance: To find live server errors and warnings, call open_cloud_invoke with the Places API's GameServers ListGameServerLogs method. Read its parameters with http_get first. The server ID is the same as game.JobId. Each log includes UniverseId, PlaceId, and PlaceVersion. Logs take about 3 minutes to show up, so wait before you decide a server has no logs.

features.name: Shop personalized in-game storefront
features.summary: Roblox builds each game a personalized Shop of its passes and Listed developer products, with Top Picks, categories, and search. Open it from your own UI with MarketplaceService:OpenShop(player). Creators manage it in Creator Hub > Monetization > Shop.
replaces: External Purchase Settings page (replaced by Listed / Not Listed in Creator Hub)
Building a custom storefront UI for passes and developer products by hand
features.guidance: To open Shop from custom buttons, NPCs, or trigger zones, call MarketplaceService:OpenShop(player) from a Script, or from a LocalScript with LocalPlayer. The script needs the PromptExternalPurchase capability. Shop purchases go through ProcessReceipt, so implement it, and ask the user to set listing status, categories, and the global Shop button in Creator Hub > Monetization > Shop.

features.name: Avatar Joint Upgrade and AnimationConstraints
features.summary: R15 characters get AnimationConstraint joints, not Motor6Ds, unless StarterPlayer.AvatarJointUpgrade is Disabled (forced end of 2026). Workspace.ImprovedAnimationConstraint adds Angular/Linear Strength and Damping to non-kinematic joints; default July 21, forced Sept 15, 2026.
replaces: Motor6D character joints
Scripts that read or set Motor6D C0, C1, Part0 or Part1 on character joints
Procedural animation that sets Motor6D.C0 every frame in RenderStepped
Moving RigAttachment.CFrame or Attachment0.CFrame for procedural animation
Setting joint C0 or Attachment CFrame on the server to replicate procedural animation
Hand-built ragdolls that swap Motor6Ds for BallSocketConstraints
Welds connecting Rigid Accessories to body parts
Directly indexing avatar Attachments, such as head.FaceCenterAttachment or UpperTorso.NeckRigAttachment
Non-recursive FindFirstChild calls for avatar Attachments
Legacy PD-controller response of non-kinematic AnimationConstraints
Re-tuning non-kinematic AnimationConstraints when connected body masses change
features.guidance: Animate joints client-side in RunService.PreSimulation via joint.Transform = offset * joint.Transform; find joints as AnimationConstraints, Attachments with FindFirstChild(name, true). For non-kinematic joints, set Workspace.ImprovedAnimationConstraint to Enabled and tune AngularStrength/AngularDamping. If AJU breaks, ask the user to set AvatarJointUpgrade to Disabled and republish.

features.name: Convert to Streaming AI skill
features.summary: An early-preview AI skill, rbx-convert-to-streaming, that converts a game to Instance Streaming through Studio MCP. It applies recommended Workspace streaming settings and ModelStreamingMode, sets LOD to SLIM, adds WaitForChild calls and nil checks, and adds replication foci.
replaces: Converting a game to Instance Streaming by hand
Setting ModelStreamingMode on each model by hand
Adding WaitForChild calls and nil checks by hand for streaming
features.guidance: When a game should use or improve streaming, suggest this skill. Ask the user to back up or copy the game first, turn on rbx-convert-to-streaming in Studio Assistant settings > Skills, then run /rbx-convert-to-streaming in their MCP client. Afterward, playtest with start_stop_play and the playtest subagent, because the skill only edits the place in Studio and can make mistakes.

features.name: ScriptDebuggerService debugger Luau API
features.summary: ScriptDebuggerService is a beta, plugin-security Luau API that controls the Studio debugger. It sets conditional breakpoints and logpoints, reads the call stack and variables of paused threads, and steps or resumes execution. Agents use it through the execute_luau MCP tool.
replaces: Temporary print() calls added to scripts for debugging
Setting breakpoints and stepping by hand in the Studio debugger
features.guidance: Via execute_luau, call ScriptDebuggerService:AddBreakpoint(script, {Line = n, Condition = "..."}), using LogMessage and ContinueExecution = true for logpoints, or SetExceptionBreakMode, then start_stop_play. In the OnStopped callback, read GetStackTrace and GetRootVariables and return an Enum.DebuggerResumeType. It's Studio-only and never pauses published games.

features.name: Community owner as a Community property, not rank 255
features.summary: Community (group) ownership is now a property of the Community, not the legacy rank-255 Owner role. That role keeps its name but has no permissions, and rank 255 is no longer reserved. Read the Owner field from GroupService:GetGroupInfoAsync to find the owner.
replaces: Treating group rank 255 as the Community owner
Checking for a role named "Owner" to find the Community owner
features.guidance: To find a Community's owner, call GroupService:GetGroupInfoAsync and read the Owner field of the result. Don't treat rank 255 or a role named "Owner" as ownership. Use script_grep for 255 and GetRankInGroup, then rewrite those owner checks with multi_edit. Outside the engine, call Open Cloud GetGroup with open_cloud_invoke and read its owner field.

features.name: Studio Script Sync
features.summary: A Studio tool that keeps Script, LocalScript, ModuleScript, and Folder instances in two-way sync with Luau files on the local drive. Developers can then edit code in external editors like VS Code, use linters and formatters, and check code into external version control such as Git.
replaces: Copying script source between Studio and local files by hand
Using Rojo only to edit scripts in an external editor
features.guidance: No MCP tool starts sync. When the user wants to edit scripts as files or use Git, ask them to right-click a Folder of scripts in the Explorer, choose Sync to..., and pick a disk directory. Keep editing synced scripts with script_read and multi_edit, since Studio edits sync to the files. It's a Studio editing tool, so it doesn't change how published experiences run.

features.name: Roblox Connect calling APIs sunset
features.summary: The Roblox Connect calling APIs on SocialService, such as CanSendCallInviteAsync and PromptPhoneBook, stop working on July 15, 2026. After that, the phonebook shows players an error dialog, callbacks don't fire, and every call invite is ineligible.
features.guidance: Don't build calling or phonebook flows. Use script_grep to find these APIs, then remove or guard that code and any call UI with multi_edit before July 15, 2026. After that date CanSendCallInviteAsync always returns false. No Engine API replaces them. For private voice, Roblox suggests Party Voice, which is a player feature and not a scripting API.

features.name: Automatic Translations player setting
features.summary: Players can turn on Automatic Translations. Roblox then machine-translates in-game text, game names, and descriptions that have no translation yet, and never overrides manual translations. Set GuiBase2d.AutoLocalize to false on text that must stay untranslated.
features.guidance: Assume any text without a translation may be auto-translated, even if the game has no languages set up. On GUI objects whose text must never be translated, such as character names or foreign signs, set AutoLocalize = false with execute_luau in the Edit datamodel. To keep a game title as is, ask the user to save a blank or unchanged manual translation in Creator Hub.

features.name: Scoped User IDs (Player.User)
features.summary: Player.User returns a User value tied to a player's per-game Scoped User ID. Engine APIs such as MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync now accept User values as well as numeric IDs. From the October 2026 rollout, players new to a game get a Scoped ID.
features.guidance: Code and DataStores need no changes, since Player.UserId keeps working. APIs such as MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync and BadgeService:UserHasBadgeAsync accept a Player.User value or a numeric ID. From October 2026, IDs of players new to a game only mean something inside that game, so don't use them to match players across games or in external services.

features.name: Improved physics replication
features.summary: Workspace.ImprovedPhysicsReplication switches physics to a new replication pipeline with eventual consistency, so packet drops don't lose updates. It rolled out globally on 15 June 2026. A temporary Disabled option lets a place opt out.
features.guidance: Expect improved physics replication to be on in Studio and in published experiences. If a physics regression shows up, such as unanchored parts freezing during network ownership changes, ask the user to set Workspace.ImprovedPhysicsReplication to Disabled in the Properties window and file a bug report, because Disabled is temporary. Measure physics network traffic with the Instance State Replication (ISR) stats.

features.name: Ban API device blocking (ApplyDeviceBlock)
features.summary: Players:BanAsync takes a new ApplyDeviceBlock field. Set it to true to also block the banned user's device from rejoining the experience, so they can't come straight back on an alt account from the same device. It blocks desktop devices only, for 24 hours.
features.guidance: To block the device too, add ApplyDeviceBlock = true to the config table you pass to Players:BanAsync in server code. It only blocks a user who is in the experience when you ban them. It only works through the engine's BanAsync. To lift a block, call Players:UnbanAsync in the engine, because unbanning through Open Cloud or the Creator Hub doesn't lift it yet.

features.name: LogService structured logging methods
features.summary: LogService:Output, Info, Warn, Error and Log take a message template such as "Hello {name}" and a context table. The context can be expanded in the F9 Developer Console and Studio Output, and Creator Analytics groups errors by template.
replaces: Building log messages with string.format or concatenation inside print or warn
Printing per-player debug data as flat text
features.guidance: To log values, get LogService and call, for example, LogService:Info("{player} leveled up", {player = name, stats = {level = 42}}) instead of formatting the values into print or warn. Keep the template constant and put the changing values in the context so Analytics groups the logs. print, warn and error still work, and get_console_output shows the results.

features.name: GetProductInfo Creator.Id returns 0 for groups
features.summary: Starting July 6, 2026, the Creator.Id field returned by MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync and GetProductInfo will be 0 for group creators. For users it stays the userId. Read Creator.CreatorType and Creator.CreatorTargetID to identify the creator.
replaces: Reading info.Creator.Id from GetProductInfo results to identify the creator
features.guidance: Don't read info.Creator.Id from product info. From July 6, 2026 it's 0 for group creators. Use info.Creator.CreatorType together with info.Creator.CreatorTargetID instead. Call MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync in pcall, not the deprecated GetProductInfo. To find code to update, run script_grep for Creator.Id.

features.name: Extended Services for Compute
features.summary: Extended Services for Compute is an opt-in Creator Hub service, turned on as Cores Quota, that more than doubles per-player server CPU for physics-heavy or server-authoritative games. Each month the first 100K playtime hours are free, then it costs $0.001 per playtime hour.
replaces: Cutting server-side physics or simulation work only because the game hits server CPU limits
features.guidance: No MCP tool turns this on. Suggest it only when live servers hit CPU limits, for example when server heartbeat drops, the simulation stutters, or a Monitoring > Performance insight recommends it, and consider optimizing server scripts first. Ask the user to enroll in Extended Services, then turn on Cores Quota for chosen Places on the game's Extended Services page and set a monthly budget.

features.name: Studio network simulation (latency, jitter, loss)
features.summary: Studio can now simulate latency, jitter and packet loss on each packet during playtests, so you can test how a game behaves on real-world connections. Set it under Studio Settings > Network, or from scripts during a test session through the NetworkSettings class.
replaces: NetworkSettings.IncomingReplicationLag
Testing network-sensitive gameplay only on a fast local connection
features.guidance: To test Server Authority, UnreliableRemoteEvent or hit registration under lag, ask the user to set inbound/outbound delay, jitter and packet loss in Studio Settings > Network. Or set them through NetworkSettings with execute_luau during a playtest (check the property names with http_get). Use 50ms in and 50ms out with 10ms jitter for a good connection. Don't combine this with IncomingReplicationLag.

features.name: Studio testing APIs: tests, device sim, virtual input
features.summary: StudioTestService runs Play Solo, Run and multiplayer tests (ExecuteMultiplayerTestAsync, up to 8 clients) from plugins and returns the result passed to EndTest. StudioDeviceSimulatorService scripts device simulation, and VirtualInput sends simulated mouse and keyboard input.
replaces: Starting play tests by hand and playing through to reach a specific part of the game
Starting multiplayer Server and Clients tests by hand
Switching simulated devices and orientations by hand in the Device Simulator
Clicking through UI menus by hand to test them
features.guidance: Plugins run tests with StudioTestService:ExecutePlayModeAsync, ExecuteRunModeAsync or ExecuteMultiplayerTestAsync (up to 8 clients); each returns what the test passes to EndTest. Set devices with StudioDeviceSimulatorService:SetDeviceAsync and SetOrientationAsync, and script input with UserInputService:CreateVirtualInput. Use user_mouse_input/user_keyboard_input for one-off input.

features.name: Paid Random Items policy and odds disclosure
features.summary: Roblox has clarified its rules for Paid Random Items, meaning random outcomes bought with Robux or with currency bought with Robux. Games must check PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync for ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted and IsPaidItemTradingAllowed, and show numerical odds before purchase.
replaces: Selling eggs, crates, spins or luck boosts without a PolicyService eligibility check
Allowing trades of paid items without checking IsPaidItemTradingAllowed
Showing rarity labels or an icon alone instead of numerical odds before purchase
features.guidance: Before offering a Paid Random Item (eggs, crates, luck boosts), call PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync and hide it or offer an alternative if ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted is true; gate paid-item trading on IsPaidItemTradingAllowed. Show numeric odds for every outcome before purchase. No MCP tool runs Studio's Player Emulator; ask the user to toggle these flags in it to test.

features.name: Multi-touch simulation in Device Emulator
features.summary: Studio's Device Emulator simulates multi-touch gestures with a mouse, so you can test pinching, rotating, and two-finger panning on PC while playtesting as a phone or tablet. It now has a refreshed device list and customizable gesture shortcuts.
replaces: Publishing and testing on a physical phone or tablet to check pinch, rotate, and two-finger pan gestures
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs this. When a game uses pinch, rotate, or two-finger pan, ask the user to pick a phone or tablet in Test > Device Emulator and playtest. They drag while holding Alt/Opt to pinch or rotate, or Alt/Opt+Shift to pan with two fingers, and can rebind these in Studio's Shortcuts menu. It only affects Studio playtests, not published experiences.

features.name: UI Styling and Transitions (StyleSheet, StyleRule)
features.summary: UI Styling applies UI property overrides from StyleRules in a StyleSheet, attached with a StyleLink. StyleRule:SetPropertyTransitions adds TweenInfo-based transitions that animate styled properties when a Tag or GuiState changes. Both work in published experiences.
replaces: Scripts that loop over GUI descendants to set colors and fonts
Copying the same visual properties onto each UI instance by hand
The :Pressed selector (use :Press)
TweenService:Create calls in MouseEnter/MouseLeave or press handlers for hover and press UI motion
features.guidance: With execute_luau, build StyleRules (Selector: class, .Tag, >, >>, :Hover, :Press) in a StyleSheet and parent a StyleLink to a ScreenGui; rules skip properties changed from defaults. For hover or press motion, call StyleRule:SetPropertyTransitions with TweenInfo values, "*" as the default, instead of TweenService in input handlers. No MCP tool opens the Style Editor, so ask the user.

features.name: GetFriendsWhoPlayedAsync for friend leaderboards
features.summary: Player:GetFriendsWhoPlayedAsync returns the user IDs of a player's friends who have played this universe. You only look up scores for those friends, which makes friend leaderboards cheaper. GlobalDataStore:BatchGetAsync reads many ordered data store keys in one call.
replaces: Players:GetFriendsAsync followed by a DataStore read for every friend on the list
One GlobalDataStore:GetAsync call per friend when reading leaderboard scores
features.guidance: For friend leaderboards or 'friends who play' menus, call player:GetFriendsWhoPlayedAsync() inside pcall and look up scores only for the IDs it returns. Read several ordered data store keys at once with BatchGetAsync. Cache the results instead of refreshing every frame or every time the UI opens, and on failure show cached data or hide the friends UI rather than blocking gameplay.

features.name: Universal Importer, Import Queue, and Scale Factor
features.summary: The Universal Importer (Import Queue) imports and uploads several .obj, .fbx, .gltf, image, audio, and video files at once. Since June 16, 2026, non-Stud units convert at 25:7 studs per meter (was 20:1), and a Scale Factor under File Geometry multiplies that conversion. Only the user can run it.
replaces: Importing and uploading 3D files one at a time with the 3D Importer
Legacy Bulk Importer for images, audio, and video
Rescaling meshes by hand after import because meter-authored content came in about 5.6x too large under the old 20:1 ratio
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs the Universal Importer. Ask the user to press Import (ribbon, File > Import, or Ctrl/Cmd-M), add the files, pick the source unit and File Geometry Scale Factor (5.6 with a non-Stud unit restores the old 20:1 size), click Import, and paste each Copy AssetId to you. Imported models are already in the workspace; pass other IDs to insert_asset.

features.name: Procedural Models (ProceduralModel)
features.summary: ProceduralModel is a container that reruns a Generator ModuleScript's OnGenerate function to rebuild its contents when its Size or attributes change. Agents can create one with the generate_procedural_model MCP tool, and creators can share them on Creator Store.
replaces: Hand-building size and count variants of repetitive models such as ladders, stairs, bridges and foliage
Hand-written plugins or scripts that delete and rebuild a model when its parameters change
features.guidance: Call generate_procedural_model (optionally with a store_image reference image) and wait_job_finished, or point Generator at a ModuleScript returning Attributes and OnGenerate(parameters, targetContainer) that writes only into targetContainer. Changing Size or attributes on the server regenerates it in live games, and generation works in Team Create.

features.name: Robux Transfers API (PromptRobuxTransferAsync)
features.summary: MarketplaceService:PromptRobuxTransferAsync opens a Roblox UI for sending Robux to another player as a tip or donation, with limits of 5,000 Robux a day and 10,000 a month for 2SV accounts. From May 29, 2026, games can't sell other games' passes or developer products.
replaces: Selling another game's passes or developer products inside your game to send donations or tips
Affiliate sales of other games' passes and developer products
features.guidance: Build tipping and donations with MarketplaceService:PromptRobuxTransferAsync, then confirm the transfer and grant any rewards in a MarketplaceService:BindReceiptHandler handler. From May 29, 2026, don't prompt passes or developer products that belong to another game. Test purchases with Studio's free purchase feature instead of cross-selling.

features.name: Team Test remote breakpoints
features.summary: A Studio beta that lets you set breakpoints on server scripts during Team Test sessions, so you can debug server logic live in a collaborative session without leaving Studio. Only the breakpoints of the user who started the session apply.
replaces: Debugging Team Test server scripts with print statements and output logs
features.guidance: No MCP tool sets breakpoints. When server logic needs debugging in Team Test, ask the user to check Remote Breakpoints in File > Beta Features, save, restart Studio if prompted, start the Team Test and set the breakpoints themselves. It's a Studio debugging tool and doesn't affect published experiences. Use get_console_output to read logs.

features.name: Creator Store asset sandboxing
features.summary: Studio now sandboxes assets inserted from the Creator Store. It blocks LoadUnownedAsset (require(id), LoadAssetAsync), LoadAsset, LoadString, CapabilityControl and getfenv/setfenv, and blocked calls error in Output. Workspace.SandboxedInstanceMode enables per-instance overrides.
replaces: Manually auditing Creator Store assets for hidden require(id), loadstring or getfenv/setfenv backdoors
features.guidance: Inserted Creator Store assets are sandboxed: their scripts can't use require(id), LoadAssetAsync, loadstring or get/setfenv, or require unsandboxed ModuleScripts or fire unsandboxed remotes and bindables. After start_stop_play, read capability errors with get_console_output. For overrides on trusted assets only, ask the user to set Workspace.SandboxedInstanceMode to Experimental.

features.name: Avatar Auto-Setup: clothing, eyebrows, decal faces
features.summary: Studio's Avatar Auto-Setup sets up a body, clothing, and accessories from a selected folder, reusing parts you provide. It now sets up eyebrows and eyelashes, converts decal-style faces to Dynamic Heads, builds R15 rigs with optional finger and spine joints, and processes clothing in parallel.
replaces: Running Avatar Auto-Setup separately for the body and for each clothing item or accessory
Letting Auto-Setup regenerate a body or head you've already rigged and skinned
Setting up a body again just to set up clothing or a rigid accessory for it
Setting up eyebrows and eyelashes by hand as layered accessories that fit different heads
Building eyeball and mouthbag meshes, cages, and FACS data by hand to turn a decal-style face into a Dynamic Head
Adding spine, clavicle, head, finger, and toe joints by hand to an Auto-Setup R15 rig
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs Avatar Auto-Setup; generate_avatar covers prompt avatars. Use execute_luau to put meshes in one folder, then ask the user to select it, run Auto-Setup, and click Setup. Have them pick Eye Layered for eyebrows or eyelashes and, in settings, turn on Handle face as a 2D decal for heads without eyeball or mouthbag meshes, or Create R15 with optional joints for fingers, toes, and spine.

features.name: SLIM (Scalable Lightweight Interactive Models)
features.summary: SLIM builds composite, multi-level LoD versions of models in the cloud and shows them when the models are streamed out (Model.LevelOfDetail = SLIM). Workspace.EnableSLIMAvatars extends it to animated R15 platform avatars. Both need StreamingEnabled.
replaces: Enum.ModelLevelOfDetail.StreamingMesh
features.guidance: Use execute_luau in Edit to set Workspace.StreamingEnabled = true, LevelOfDetail = Enum.ModelLevelOfDetail.SLIM on Models (not StreamingMesh) and on any StarterCharacter, and Workspace.EnableSLIMAvatars to Enabled for R15 player avatars. Both work in published experiences. Ask the user to test avatars in Team Test or in a Server & Clients test with 2+ clients.

features.name: Publishing eligibility requirements for games
features.summary: Publishing to 16+ and Trusted Friends needs an age check. To reach Kids and Select (under 16), you also need a refundable 1,000 Robux fee per game or 2 months of Plus/Premium, plus 500 highly engaged players in 60 days. 'Private' games are now Edit-permission only.
replaces: Sharing a 'Private' game with Playtest-permission users
features.guidance: If publishing in Studio or via open_cloud_invoke fails on eligibility, don't retry: ask the user to meet the requirements at https://create.roblox.com/settings/eligibility/publishing-permissions. To share with playtesters, ask the user to set Audience to Limited > Playtesters, since 'Private' only admits Edit-permission holders. Creator Hub's Audience Reach tab shows Kids/Select eligibility.

features.name: Reimport
features.summary: Studio's Reimport updates an imported Model, SurfaceAppearance, or Decal in place from its source files, keeping Studio edits like welds and scripts, including rigs, bones, joints, cages, and dynamic heads. It reuses Import 3D's settings.
replaces: Deleting an imported model and importing the updated FBX/glTF file again, then redoing Studio setup work
Uploading each SurfaceAppearance or Decal texture map again by hand
Manually running Reimport in Studio after every change to an external source file
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs Reimport. When an imported FBX/glTF file or texture changes, ask the user to right-click the Model, SurfaceAppearance, or Decal, select Reimport (Alt+Shift+R), and pick the file, preset, and upload account or group if Configure opens. Don't rename or move its MeshParts (Reimport matches them by name) or add Bones in Studio (Reimport deletes bones missing from the file).

features.name: Scene Analysis tool and SceneAnalysisService
features.summary: Scene Analysis is a Studio treemap that shows script, audio and animation memory, unparented instances, instance composition and triangles, and traces usage back to instances. SceneAnalysisService returns the same data as nested tables.
replaces: Hand-written scripts that count instances, triangles or particle emitters to audit scene complexity
Guessing memory usage per script, sound or animation from Dev Console totals alone
