features.guidance: Get the SceneAnalysisService method names from its reference page with http_get, then call them through execute_luau to read memory and instance data as nested tables, ideally during a playtest started with start_stop_play. No MCP tool opens the treemap: after big code or asset changes, ask the user to open Window > Performance Summary > Scene Analysis during a playtest.

features.name: Asset privacy and sharing for Image, Mesh, Decal assets
features.summary: Asset Privacy is fully released and on by default for new accounts and groups. New Image, Mesh, and Decal assets are Restricted (private) and get permission checks when loaded or inserted. AssetService:CreateEditableMeshAsync and CreateEditableImageAsync also load shared assets.
replaces: Transferring asset ownership to the experience owner so EditableMesh or EditableImage can load it
Re-uploading a contractor's or collaborator's mesh or image from the experience owner's account
Sharing assets or setting them to Open Use one at a time on each asset's Creator Hub Configure page
features.guidance: Inserting a Restricted asset into a place with insert_asset gives that experience permission, so the asset then works when published. Call save_place first and check get_console_output for permission errors. For assets you don't own, including with CreateEditableMeshAsync or CreateEditableImageAsync, ask the user to share them in Creator Hub or Asset Manager. Only the user can set Open Use, and it can't be undone.

features.name: Adaptive Animation (HumanoidRigDescription)
features.summary: Adaptive Animation retargets animations between custom rigs and R15/R6 avatars with a HumanoidRigDescription and per-hand DigitsRigDescriptions. R15 platform avatars can now add optional Bone joints: fingers, Spine, Chest, clavicles, HeadBase and toe base.
replaces: Authoring separate animations for each custom rig skeleton
Hand-animating fingers per rig structure
HRD Pelvis joint mapping (now Spine)
HRD LeftToes/RightToes mappings (now LeftToeBase/RightToeBase)
Custom Humanoid rig type in the 3D Importer
Hard-coded character DataModel paths in scripts, which break under the Avatar Joint Upgrade
features.guidance: If a custom character's Model has no HumanoidRigDescription (check with inspect_instance), ask the user to import it with the Avatar Joint Upgrade (AJU) on, then click Adaptive Animation in the Avatar tab and Create to add the HRD and DRDs. Optional joints use Bones, so use script_grep to find hard-coded character paths that break under AJU. Map beta Pelvis joints to Spine.

features.name: Age Check API (Player:PromptAgeCheck)
features.summary: Player:PromptAgeCheck() opens the age check flow from inside your game, and Player.AgeChecked (Enum.AgeCheckStatus) shows whether the player completed it. Use them to grow the segment of age-checked US 18+ players whose spend earns the higher US 18+ DevEx rate.
replaces: Relying only on players who already age-checked outside the game
features.guidance: Call player:PromptAgeCheck() on a deliberate player action, such as claiming a small optional reward, not on spawn. It doesn't yield and returns nothing. Read the read-only, replicated player.AgeChecked and compare it to Enum.AgeCheckStatus.Checked. Gate only optional rewards or zones behind Checked, never core gameplay, and treat Unchecked as a normal state.

features.name: Mesh Streaming and improved cloud LoDs
features.summary: Mesh Streaming streams improved cloud-generated mesh LoDs based on scene importance, within a mesh memory budget. Published experiences opt in by setting Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLods to Enabled. It's expected to become the default around July 2026.
replaces: Setting MeshPart.RenderFidelity per part to control mesh LoD quality
features.guidance: Ask the user to set Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLods to Enabled (Workspace > Behavior), restart Studio, test, and publish. It works in published experiences, with or without Workspace.StreamingEnabled. When it's enabled, MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored, so stop setting it to control mesh quality. This becomes the default around July 2026.

features.name: MessagingService unified Open Cloud rate limits
features.summary: From May 11, 2026, messages published through the MessagingService Open Cloud API count toward the same limits as in-experience MessagingService, such as 1kB per message and per-server and per-topic limits.
replaces: Treating MessagingService Open Cloud API rate limits as separate from in-experience MessagingService limits
features.guidance: From May 11, 2026, count Open Cloud MessagingService publishes (for example through open_cloud_invoke) and in-experience MessagingService usage toward one shared budget. Keep messages under 1kB, and plan around the per-server send, per-topic receive and subscription limits on the MessagingService reference page.

features.name: Studio MCP subagents: Data Model Search and Playtest
features.summary: The subagent MCP tool's explore type, the Data Model Search subagent, investigates a place on its own thread. Several can run at once, and each returns only its findings. The playtest type is still a beta. Quick connect in Assistant Settings connects external MCP clients to Studio.
replaces: Running many search_game_tree, script_read, and script_grep calls in the main agent's context to investigate a large place
Running each playtest yourself with start_stop_play, character_navigation, user_keyboard_input, and user_mouse_input in the main agent's context
Editing MCP client config files by hand to connect a supported client to Studio
features.guidance: To investigate a large place, call the subagent MCP tool with type explore and one scoped question per call. Run several in parallel, and say what to return, such as exact paths. Type playtest is still a beta: ask the user to check Playtest Agent in File > Beta Features, then confirm any Pass with get_console_output or screen_capture. Neither type affects published experiences.

features.name: Cookie-based web API restrictions
features.summary: Roblox is restricting cookie-based web APIs: removing unauthenticated access, cutting rate limits to human-usage levels (many on 4 May 2026) and sunsetting endpoints. Engine APIs such as BadgeService and Open Cloud are the supported way to access user data.
replaces: Calling cookie-based web APIs (apis.roblox.com endpoints used by the website and app) from game code or tools
Scraping user data such as friends, badges or profiles through unofficial endpoints
features.guidance: Don't write game code or tools that call cookie-based web endpoints. Use Engine APIs in game code, such as BadgeService:UserHasBadgeAsync or BadgeService:CheckUserBadgesAsync for badges, and Open Cloud through open_cloud_invoke for tools, such as Groups GetGroup. Many endpoints drop to low cookie rate limits on 4 May 2026, and script_grep finds code that calls them.

features.name: Automated RTBF processing for Data Stores
features.summary: A beta where you define deletion templates with a {UserId} token, such as PlayerData_{UserId}. Roblox then deletes the matching data store entries automatically when a user files a Right to be Forgotten request. You set templates in Creator Hub or through the Open Cloud Configs API.
replaces: Custom RTBF webhook that deletes a user's Data Store entries
Deleting a user's Data Store keys by hand for each RTBF request
features.guidance: Use script_grep for GetDataStore and GetOrderedDataStore to find store names, keys, or scopes that contain the user ID, then propose templates such as player_{UserId}. Ask the user to add them in Creator Hub > Data Stores Manager > RTBF Deletion, or use open_cloud_invoke to write key user_data_templates in the DataStoresConfig repository with the Configs API. The beta deletes live data.

features.name: ClientAnimatorThrottling always on
features.summary: From April 29, 2026, ClientAnimatorThrottling is always on: the engine updates animations less often for far or hidden characters, local client-only ones included. Workspace.ClientAnimatorThrottling no longer toggles it. Animator.PreferLodEnabled asks the engine not to throttle a rig.
replaces: Turning off throttling for the whole place with Workspace.ClientAnimatorThrottling
Spawning characters only on the client to keep their animations from being throttled
features.guidance: From April 29, 2026, don't use Workspace.ClientAnimatorThrottling to turn off throttling. For a character whose animation must stay smooth, set its Animator's PreferLodEnabled to false. This is only a hint, and the engine can still throttle under heavy load. Test custom animation systems and R6/R15 rigs in a playtest (start_stop_play), local characters included.

features.name: StyleQuery responsive UI styling
features.summary: StyleQuery is a new instance that turns on StyleRules only when conditions are met: an element's size or aspect ratio, or the player's input, viewport size, reduced motion setting or text size. Rules target active queries with @ selectors, so responsive UI needs no scripts.
replaces: Scripts that listen to UserInputService.PreferredInput and swap UI properties such as input hint images
Scripts that watch GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize to restyle UI at different sizes
features.guidance: To restyle UI by input or text size, nest StyleRules with built-in selectors such as @PreferredInputTouch, @PreferredInputGamepad, @PreferredInputKeyboardAndMouse or @PreferredTextSizeLarge under the element's StyleRule (create them with execute_luau). For size or aspect-ratio conditions, parent a StyleQuery to the GuiBase2d, set MinSize, MaxSize, or AspectRatioRange with StyleQuery:SetCondition, and target it with @QueryName. This works in published experiences.

features.name: Signals reactive state library and rocale-cli
features.summary: Roblox released Signals, an open-source reactive state library and alternative to Rodux, on Wally and the Creator Store. It also released rocale-cli, which uploads a local Rojo project, runs it through Open Cloud Luau Execution and sends output back to a terminal, agent or CI.
replaces: Rodux for managing complex derived state
Testing local Luau projects by hand in Studio instead of from the terminal or CI
features.guidance: For complex derived game or UI state, consider Signals: get it from the Creator Store with search_asset and insert_asset, or from Wally under roblox/. To run a local Rojo project in the cloud, pass place ID, universe ID and API key as named parameters to rocale-cli and print results. Ask the user for a key with universe-places:write and luau-execution-sessions:write.

features.name: VideoFrame audio rolloff and Volume cap
features.summary: VideoFrame now has RollOffMaxDistance, RollOffMinDistance and RollOffMode, which control how video audio fades over distance, the same way they do on Sound. Since April 22, 2026, VideoFrame.Volume is capped at 10 instead of 100.
replaces: Setting VideoFrame.Volume above 10 to make up for having no rolloff control
features.guidance: To control how a VideoFrame's audio fades with distance, set RollOffMinDistance, RollOffMaxDistance and RollOffMode (an Enum.RollOffMode) the same way you would on a Sound. Keep VideoFrame.Volume between 0 and 10. Higher values don't error, but they're set to 10. Use script_grep to find scripts that set Volume above 10.

features.name: Character Controller Library (AvatarAbilities)
features.summary: The Character Controller Library (AvatarAbilities on ControllerManager) is out of beta for live experiences. It replaces Humanoid movement with Luau Walk, Run, Jump, Swim, Climb and Sit abilities. Opt in through Avatar Settings and tune controller properties such as GroundController.Friction.
replaces: Hard-coded Humanoid state machine for character movement
Hand-written Luau state machines driving ControllerManager
Hand-written CFrame math to keep characters moving with platforms and vehicles
features.guidance: Ask the user to save or publish (save_place saves), then select Character Controller Library in Avatar Settings > Movement. Tune GroundController and AirController properties and Ability attributes under Ability/SyncedState with scripts or execute_luau. It works live; it sets Player.DevEnableMouseLock false, so set it true at runtime to restore Shift Lock.

features.name: ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances query filters
features.summary: RaycastParams and OverlapParams have new ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances properties. You can set both on one query, so a single query can include a folder but skip part of it. They're faster than FilterDescendantsInstances, which will be deprecated at a later date.
replaces: RaycastParams.FilterDescendantsInstances
RaycastParams.FilterType
OverlapParams.FilterDescendantsInstances
OverlapParams.FilterType
RaycastParams:AddToFilter
OverlapParams:AddToFilter
Running several raycasts to combine include and exclude filters
features.guidance: In new raycast, shapecast and overlap code, set ExcludeInstances and/or IncludeInstances instead of FilterDescendantsInstances and FilterType. You can set both at once. IncludeInstances = nil includes everything and {} includes nothing. Instead of AddToFilter, insert into a table and assign it to ExcludeInstances again. Use script_grep to find old filters when the user asks to migrate.

features.name: Player segments: spender, active payer, tenure
features.summary: AnalyticsService:GetPlayerSegmentsAsync(player) returns a dictionary of a player's segments as enums: platform spender status, in-experience active payer status, and tenure (time since first play). Use it to personalize gameplay, offers and onboarding.
features.guidance: Call AnalyticsService:GetPlayerSegmentsAsync(player) and branch on the returned dictionary, for example extra tutorials for new players or a Robux option for active payers. A segment can be missing, so handle absent keys. Before writing code, use http_get on the AnalyticsService reference page to get the exact dictionary keys and enum names from its code snippet.

features.name: Avatar Makeup (WrapTextureTransfer)
features.summary: Avatar Makeup is fully launched, with FaceMakeup, LipMakeup and EyeMakeup asset types. A WrapTextureTransfer under a Decal fits makeup to each head's cage, AssetService:ComposeDecalAsync flattens layers into one decal, and MakeupDescription works through HumanoidDescription.
features.guidance: Imported makeup comes in as Decals with a WrapTextureTransfer child. To preview, move them into a character's Makeup folder with execute_luau, and use AssetService:ComposeDecalAsync to flatten layers. Avatars loaded through HumanoidDescription get their makeup automatically (MakeupDescription holds asset ID, order and type), so don't apply worn makeup by hand.

features.name: CreateDataModelContentAsync static mesh and image content
features.summary: AssetService:CreateDataModelContentAsync bakes an EditableMesh or EditableImage into static, opaque Content that lasts for the session. It drives MeshContent and TextureContent like an asset ID, replicates from server to clients, and needs no upload. It works in published experiences.
replaces: Keeping EditableMesh and EditableImage objects alive to drive MeshPart content after you've finished editing them
Uploading procedurally generated meshes or images as assets so they can replicate to clients
features.guidance: When you've finished editing, call AssetService:CreateDataModelContentAsync(Content.fromObject(editable)). If the result is Enum.CreateContentResult.Success, use the Content with CreateMeshPartAsync or TextureContent, then Destroy the editable to free its memory budget. Bake on the server so clients get the content, because content baked on a client stays on that client. To edit again, pass the Content to CreateEditableMeshAsync or CreateEditableImageAsync.

features.name: Chat preset system guidelines
features.summary: Updated rules for custom chat presets used for gameplay coordination: filter each one with TextService:FilterStringAsync, allow one send per 10 seconds, use 12 or fewer per universe, and leave out terminal punctuation and social phrases. Existing systems must comply by 2026-04-26.
replaces: Custom preset or quick-chat systems used for social communication, such as greetings, Yes/No, or personal questions
Unfiltered, unlimited, or unthrottled developer-defined chat presets
features.guidance: Only build a custom preset system if the game needs one, and make it comply by 2026-04-26: 12 or fewer gameplay presets per universe (no greetings, Yes/No, or terminal punctuation), each filtered with TextService:FilterStringAsync (once at load is fine), and a 10-second rate limit per send. Label presets as system presets and make them look different from Roblox chat.

features.name: Voice Chat in 100-player servers and on consoles
features.summary: VoiceChatService voice chat now works in servers of up to 100 users, up from 50, and on PlayStation and Xbox. Since 2026-05-07, voice is on by default for age-checked 13+ users in new experiences with a maximum of 100 players.
replaces: Keeping voice experiences at 50 or fewer players per server
features.guidance: Voice works on consoles and in servers of up to 100 players, so don't assume it's off there. Use VoiceChatService, because TextChatService doesn't cover voice. New experiences with up to 100 players have voice on by default for age-checked 13+ users. To turn it on or off, ask the user to change Enable Voice Chat (formerly Enable Microphone) in the experience's communication settings.

features.name: Studio MCP playtest, screenshot, and generation tools
features.summary: Studio's built-in MCP server lets agents playtest and build: start_stop_play, get_console_output, user_mouse_input, user_keyboard_input and character_navigation run and drive playtests, screen_capture shows the viewport, and generate_mesh and generate_material make assets from prompts.
replaces: Asking the user to press Play and paste Output logs back to the agent
Checking changes only in Edit mode without running a playtest
Asking the user to click through UI or move the character during a playtest
Asking the user to screenshot or describe what the playtest viewport shows
Asking the user to find and insert Creator Store models by hand
Asking the user to model placeholder props or make material variants by hand
Connecting external AI clients through the open-source studio-rust-mcp-server instead of the built-in server
features.guidance: Playtest with get_studio_state and start_stop_play, drive it with user_mouse_input, user_keyboard_input or character_navigation, and check it with execute_luau, get_console_output and screen_capture before fixing scripts in Edit mode. Make assets with generate_mesh, generate_material, or search_asset then insert_asset. With several Studio windows open, call list_roblox_studios first.

features.name: Multiple roles per Community member
features.summary: Community (group) members can now hold several roles at once, and their permissions add together. New Open Cloud endpoints, Assign Role Group Membership and Unassign Role Group Membership, add or remove one role without touching the member's other roles.
replaces: PATCH Update Group Membership to change a member's role, which now removes all their roles and sets only the one you specify
Giving a member one role that combines several roles' permissions
features.guidance: To grant or remove one role, such as for a level milestone or the end of an event, call Assign Role Group Membership or Unassign Role Group Membership with open_cloud_invoke or from the experience. Use PATCH Update Group Membership only when you want to replace all of a member's roles with one. GET ListGroupMemberships returns the highest-ranked role plus a list of the member's assigned rolesets.

features.name: Multi-line Command Bar
features.summary: The Studio Command Bar is now fully released as an embedded script editor. It has multi-line editing, linting, code completion, inline docs, Studio-wide undo/redo of what a command changes, and saved commands. It's for prototyping and bulk edits.
replaces: Keeping multi-line commands in a separate script tab and pasting them into the single-line Command Bar
features.guidance: Run Luau yourself with execute_luau, because no MCP tool uses the Command Bar. If the user wants to rerun or tweak a bulk-edit snippet, suggest they save it in the Command Bar with Ctrl+B and run it with Run or Ctrl+Return. It's a Studio-only tool and doesn't affect published experiences.

features.name: Configs and experiments (live config, A/B tests)
features.summary: Configs change in-game values and feature flags live without server restarts, and scripts read them with ConfigSnapshot:GetValue. The Open Cloud configs API creates, reads, and updates configs from code, with change history. Experiments A/B test configs.
replaces: Hard-coded tuning values that need a new publish or server restart to change
Hand-built feature flags and remote value systems
Hand-rolled A/B test bucketing
Editing configs by hand in Creator Hub or Studio for live ops
features.guidance: For live values like rewards, damage, or feature flags, create, read, or update configs with the Open Cloud configs API via open_cloud_invoke (universe:read scope to read, universe:write to publish), or ask the user to make them in Creator Hub. Read them in scripts with GetValue, added with multi_edit. Call GetValue for an experiment key only when needed, because that call enrolls the player.

features.name: Regional Pricing for passes and developer products
features.summary: From March 30, 2026, all passes use Regional Pricing by default, and creators can opt out per pass. Developer products stay opt-in. UI that shows prices must fetch them at runtime with MarketplaceService. Games with trading or gifting should use the User Price Level API.
replaces: Hard-coded Robux prices in developer product and pass shop UI
Allowing trades or gifts without checking each user's price level
features.guidance: Fetch pass and developer product prices at runtime in a LocalScript with MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync (not the deprecated GetProductInfo) or GetDeveloperProductsAsync. Never hard-code them. For developer product trades or gifts, read the regional-pricing docs with http_get and use the User Price Level API. Opting in and out is per item in the Creator Hub, so ask the user.

features.name: Place Version History
features.summary: A redesigned, dockable Place Version History in Studio. Collaborators can add notes to saved and published place versions, search those notes, and filter versions by date, save type, published saves, collaborator, or whether a save has notes.
replaces: The old Place Version History interface
Tracking place checkpoints and releases by hand outside Studio
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs Version History or adds version notes. save_place only saves a new version without notes. When the user needs a rollback, a milestone, or to find what went live, ask them to open Window > Version History (or Asset Manager > Places > right-click > View History), or to press Ctrl+Alt+S (Cmd+Option+S on Mac) to save with notes.

features.name: Badge ownership privacy restrictions
features.summary: Starting March 23, 2026, server calls to BadgeService:UserHasBadgeAsync and CheckUserBadgesAsync act as if a badge from another experience isn't awarded when the user hasn't recently been in the server. The badges.roblox.com awarded-date endpoints get privacy limits too.
replaces: Checking other experiences' badges for users who haven't recently been in the server
Unauthenticated or cookie-authenticated calls to the badges.roblox.com awarded-date endpoints
features.guidance: Starting March 23, 2026, check badges from other experiences only for players who are in the server or were there recently. Badges your own experience created still work for any user. For external tools that call badges.roblox.com awarded-date endpoints, move to the Open Cloud Badges and Inventory APIs with API keys or OAuth.

features.name: MaterialVariant AlphaMode
features.summary: A Studio beta adds MaterialVariant.AlphaMode, so the alpha channel of a MaterialVariant's ColorMap can change how the material looks, as it does with SurfaceAppearance. It also adds a new Enum.AlphaMode.Opaque option, the default, which ignores alpha.
features.guidance: Ask the user to turn on 'MaterialVariant Alpha Mode' in File > Beta Features. Then, with execute_luau, set MaterialVariant.AlphaMode on a variant whose ColorMap has an alpha channel, for example on one made by generate_material. Use Transparency to cut out shapes such as fences, but sparingly, since it costs the most. The announcement doesn't say if this works in published experiences, so treat it as Studio-only.

features.name: JSONEncode encoding of inf, -inf and NaN
features.summary: HttpService:JSONEncode now writes inf, -inf and NaN as valid JSON objects such as {"m":null,"t":"numeric","v":"inf"}, and HttpService:JSONDecode turns them back into Luau numbers. This only changes what external servers receive.
replaces: Server-side handling of non-standard inf/NaN literals or null in JSON from HttpService:JSONEncode
features.guidance: When JSONEncode output goes to a system outside Roblox, that system gets {"m":null,"t":"numeric","v":"inf"|"-inf"|"NaN"} for non-finite numbers. Either handle that shape on the server, or replace non-finite values before encoding (x ~= x for NaN, math.abs(x) == math.huge for inf). Data that goes from Roblox to Roblox, like JSONDecode round trips and data stores, works as before.

features.name: Text-to-Speech API (AudioTextToSpeech)
features.summary: Turns text into speech with 11 preset English voices and voices in 10 more languages, which you can adjust for pitch and speed. AudioTextToSpeech speaks in real time on the client. The GenerateSpeechAsset Open Cloud API saves the speech as an audio asset you can reuse.
replaces: Recording and uploading voice-over audio by hand for narration and NPC dialogue
features.guidance: Script AudioTextToSpeech on the client (it's client-only) and set VoiceId to a string that matches Player.LocaleId: "1"-"11" English; Spanish "101"/"102", German "201"/"202", Italian "301"/"302", French "401"/"402" (male/female). Keep requests to 300 characters and handle filter or moderation errors. For reused lines, call GenerateSpeechAsset via open_cloud_invoke, never with player text.

features.name: Emissive Masks
features.summary: SurfaceAppearance, MaterialVariant and TerrainDetail have EmissiveMaskContent, EmissiveStrength and EmissiveTint properties, now live in published experiences. A grayscale mask controls which parts of a surface glow, giving finer control than the Neon material.
replaces: Using Enum.Material.Neon parts to fake detailed glowing areas such as text, lights or trim
features.guidance: Set EmissiveMaskContent at edit time with execute_luau (datamodel_type Edit), or pass an EditableImage mask to AssetService:CreateSurfaceAppearanceAsync. Scripts can change EmissiveStrength (0 or higher, slider 0-40) and EmissiveTint at runtime. It works in published experiences, and the glow color comes from the ColorMap and EmissiveTint, not the mask.

features.name: Speech-to-Text API (AudioSpeechToText)
features.summary: AudioSpeechToText is now fully released. It turns microphone audio, or any other audio, into text for voice commands, subtitles, and NPC conversations. It detects English and 16 other languages on its own, and takes up to 10 seconds of audio per request.
features.guidance: Ask the user to turn on File > Game Settings > Communication > Enable Microphone. Keep VoiceChatService.UseAudioApi on and send a player's AudioDeviceInput, or other audio, to an AudioSpeechToText created in a script or the Explorer, following the tutorial's code. To keep speech private, set EnableDefaultVoice to false or disconnect AudioDeviceInput from AudioEmitter.

features.name: In-Experience Avatar and Accessory Auto Setup
features.summary: AvatarCreationService:AutoSetupAvatarAsync turns a player's simple model into a rigged, caged avatar body, and now into layered clothing and rigid accessories too, during gameplay. LoadGeneratedAvatarAsync returns a HumanoidDescription with EditableMesh and EditableImage parts you can still edit.
replaces: Setting up layered clothing and accessories by hand in Studio
features.guidance: On the server, call AvatarCreationService:AutoSetupAvatarAsync(player, {Body = bodyModel, Accessories = {{AccessoryType = Enum.AccessoryType.Shirt, IsLayered = true, Instance = model}}}) inside a pcall. Load the returned ID with LoadGeneratedAvatarAsync to get a HumanoidDescription, then publish with PromptCreateAvatarAsync. It's in Client Beta and works in published experiences.

features.name: Access Control for Places and secure server teleports
features.summary: The Direct Access to Places setting is replaced by three Access Control for Places options: Fully Open, Limited to same Universe, and Secure within Universe only. The last one blocks client-started teleports, so teleports must come from TeleportService:TeleportAsync in server scripts.
replaces: Direct Access to Places setting (on/off)
Starting TeleportService teleports from LocalScripts
features.guidance: Start teleports only from server Scripts with TeleportService:TeleportAsync(placeId, {player}). When a client needs to trigger one, have it signal the server, then check it against game progress. Use script_grep to find teleport calls in LocalScripts. Then ask the user to pick Secure within Universe only under the experience's or place's Access settings, because you can't change it.

features.name: Chat groups APIs, matchmaking and Trusted Connections
features.summary: Chat requires an age check (global since 2026-01-07). TextChatService:GetChatGroupsAsync and VoiceChatService:GetChatGroupsAsync return chat group IDs for players who can text or voice chat together. Custom Matchmaking has a TextChat signal for players who can chat.
features.guidance: Ask the user to turn on "Enable chat & voice groups APIs" in Experience Settings > Communication, which needs them to accept the responsible-use terms. Then pcall GetChatGroupsAsync(players) in a server Script and team or teleport players whose group ID arrays overlap. Groups change, so check again each time a player joins, and don't store them. If chat matters, raise the TextChat weight in Custom Matchmaking.

features.name: 4D generation with GenerateModelAsync
features.summary: Beta: GenerationService:GenerateModelAsync generates multi-mesh functional objects in-experience, such as a 5-part Car-5 car or a single-mesh Body-1, with optional Size and MaxTriangles. TextGenerator supports structured JSON output. GenerateMeshAsync stops working March 18, 2026.
replaces: GenerationService:GenerateMeshAsync
features.guidance: Use GenerationService:GenerateModelAsync with the Car-5 or Body-1 schema instead of GenerateMeshAsync, which stops working on March 18, 2026. The beta is open to all creators and works in published experiences, with no enrollment needed. Write behavior scripts that adapt to whatever geometry gets generated, and for a static mesh made in Studio at edit time, call the generate_mesh MCP tool instead.

features.name: Texture Streaming
features.summary: The engine streams texture mips automatically by object importance and the device's memory budget. It now renders images at up to 4k (4096x4096) in published experiences on MeshPart, SurfaceAppearance, Texture, Decal and MaterialVariant. No setting or API.
replaces: Texture atlases on parts that aren't batchable
Downscaling or limiting unique textures by hand to fit low-memory devices
Splitting high-detail textures across several 1k images
features.guidance: Nothing to turn on, and it isn't Workspace.StreamingEnabled, which streams instances. Upload images up to 8k (rendered at up to 4k) for MeshPart, SurfaceAppearance, Texture, Decal and MaterialVariant, using unique textures rather than atlases and near-uniform texel density. Don't preload texture assets with ContentProvider:PreloadAsync, which currently keeps streaming from working properly.

features.name: Acoustic Simulation (audio occlusion and reverb)
features.summary: With SoundService.AcousticSimulationEnabled on, 3D audio from the Advanced Audio API (audio assets, voice chat, character sounds) is muffled by walls, bends around corners and echoes off rooms in real time. It works in published experiences.
replaces: AudioEmitter.SimulationFidelity
AudioListener.SimulationFidelity
features.guidance: Set SoundService.AcousticSimulationEnabled = true (for example with execute_luau in Edit, then save_place), and play 3D audio through an AudioPlayer wired to an AudioEmitter, because Sound instances aren't simulated. Turn on SoundService.CharacterSoundsUseNewApi for character audio, and set VoiceChatService.UseAudioApi to Enabled for voice. Set BasePart.AudioCanCollide to false on parts that shouldn't block sound.

features.name: Dynamic Head migration of Classic Heads and Faces
features.summary: Classic Heads and Faces are now Dynamic Heads. AvatarEditorService searches return nothing for Face and Head asset types, and Classic assets redirect on equip. GetHeadShapesAsync, BodyPartDescription.HeadShape and HumanoidDescription.StaticFacialAnimation add head shapes and static faces.
replaces: Separate Classic Heads and Classic Faces categories in avatar editor UI
Querying Enum.AvatarAssetType.Face or Enum.AvatarAssetType.Head with SearchCatalog or GetInventory
features.guidance: SearchCatalogAsync and GetInventoryAsync return nothing for Enum.AvatarAssetType.Face or Head, so use one Heads category and filter SearchCatalogAsync by Roblox as creator. Call ConformToAvatarRulesAsync before showing an avatar. Get owned Classic head shapes with GetHeadShapesAsync, apply via BodyPartDescription.HeadShape, and use HumanoidDescription.StaticFacialAnimation to stop face animation.

features.name: Async suffix for yielding methods
features.summary: Dozens of yielding Engine methods now have Async names, such as Player:LoadCharacterAsync, Player:IsInGroupAsync and BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync. The old names are deprecated to help avoid mistakes. They still work the same way and won't be changed or removed.
replaces: Calling these yielding methods by their old names without Async, such as player:LoadCharacter() or player:IsInGroup(id)
features.guidance: In new code, use the Async names, such as player:LoadCharacterAsync(), player:IsInGroupAsync(id) and BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync. Wrap cloud calls in pcall, and wrap each call in task.spawn to run several at once. The old names still work, so only update existing scripts when the user asks (script_grep finds them). WaitForChild, InvokeServer, InvokeClient and BindableFunction:Invoke keep their names.

features.name: In-game social links sunset and TextChatService-only chat
features.summary: With age checks to chat now required, all player-to-player text has to go through TextChatService. Starting February 2026, in-game social links are no longer allowed: PolicyServiceAPI.GetExternalLinkReference returns an empty list, and AllowedExternalLinkReferences no longer permits showing links.
replaces: Showing social links (X, Discord invites) in-game based on AllowedExternalLinkReferences from PolicyServiceAPI
Custom player-to-player text systems that bypass TextChatService
features.guidance: Send all player-to-player text through TextChatService. Use TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage for announcements. Remove in-game social links and Discord invites, and don't gate them on AllowedExternalLinkReferences. Show text like "Check out our social media links on our game's page" instead. Use script_grep to find old link code.

features.name: PlayerOwnsAssetAsync inventory privacy enforcement
features.summary: Starting January 27, 2026, MarketplaceService:PlayerOwnsAssetAsync throws an error when a LocalScript checks another player's assets and that player's inventory privacy setting applies. Server calls don't change. Legacy inventory.roblox.com endpoints also enforce privacy.
replaces: Calling PlayerOwnsAssetAsync from a LocalScript to check another player's inventory
MarketplaceService:PlayerOwnsAsset
Legacy inventory.roblox.com v1 and v2 web endpoints
features.guidance: Call MarketplaceService:PlayerOwnsAssetAsync from a server Script, never from a LocalScript, and pass the result to clients that need it. Use script_grep for PlayerOwnsAsset to find client calls and move them to the server. Replace inventory.roblox.com calls with the Open Cloud Inventory endpoints, which take API keys or OAuth.

features.name: FastCluster avatar rendering optimizations
features.summary: FastCluster, which renders any Model with a Humanoid or skinned MeshPart, no longer rebuilds on Seat or weld/constraint changes, Tool equips, or Highlight changes, and builds skeletons faster. This cuts avatar framerate drops.
replaces: Avoiding Highlight effects on avatars to prevent framerate hitches
Workarounds to stop FastCluster rebuilds when seating avatars or equipping Tools
features.guidance: Give Tools and accessories you add to avatars rigid parts only, with no skinned MeshParts, and don't add or remove parts with geometry under an avatar Model when seating or welding, so neither triggers a FastCluster rebuild. Highlights on avatars no longer trigger rebuilds. Avoid frequent layered clothing swaps, respawns, and avatar scale changes, which still drop frames.

features.name: In-experience Community join prompt
features.summary: GroupService:PromptJoinAsync(groupId) is a client-only method. It shows a native prompt to join a Community (group) without leaving the experience, yields until the player chooses, and returns an Enum.GroupMembershipStatus.
replaces: Telling players to leave the experience and join the Community on the website
features.guidance: Call GroupService:PromptJoinAsync(groupId) from a LocalScript, wrapped in pcall, and branch on the result: Joined, JoinRequestPending, AlreadyMember, or None (cancelled or ineligible). To check membership on the server afterward, use GroupService:GetGroupsAsync, because Player group checks on the server can be cached for up to 60 seconds. Keep join rewards small, since players can join and then leave.

features.name: Auto-skinning leader and follower vertices
features.summary: WrapLayer.AutoSkin now supports leader and follower vertices. Leaders deform with the body mesh, and followers move with the nearest leaders, so eyebrows, eyelashes, beards and other facial accessories deform naturally on any head.
replaces: One-size-fits-all WrapLayer.AutoSkin transfer that stretched delicate facial accessories
features.guidance: Ask the user to turn on the Makeup Studio Beta in File > Beta Features. The announcement doesn't say whether it works in published experiences. Mark leader and follower vertices as the docs describe, then use execute_luau to set WrapLayer.AutoSkin to EnabledOverride. For eyelashes, set MeshPart.DoubleSided to true and SurfaceAppearance.AlphaMode to Transparency.

features.name: Product Intelligence APIs for passes and dev products
features.summary: MarketplaceService:RankProductsAsync and MarketplaceService:RecommendTopProductsAsync use machine learning to personalize which passes and developer products each player sees, so you can build stores like a 'Top Picks for You' section.
replaces: Fixed, hand-ordered lists of passes and developer products in in-experience stores
The same featured items shown to every player
features.guidance: To order your own list of passes and developer products for a player, pass an array of product identifiers to MarketplaceService:RankProductsAsync. For a 'Top Picks' section, pass an array of Enum.InfoType to MarketplaceService:RecommendTopProductsAsync, which returns up to 50 items. Roblox recommends calling these when the player joins.

features.name: Open Cloud APIs for developer products and game passes
features.summary: New Open Cloud APIs create, fetch, update, and list developer products and game passes for a universe. You can set up monetization items in code instead of by hand in Creator Hub. They support API key authentication.
replaces: Creating and editing developer products and game passes by hand in Creator Hub
features.guidance: When a game needs developer products or game passes, call open_cloud_invoke with the Open Cloud developer product or game pass APIs to create, fetch, update, or list them for the universe. Don't ask the user to set them up by hand in Creator Hub. Read the endpoints and fields with http_get from the Developer products and Game passes Cloud docs before you call them.

features.name: Groups API member list privacy and rate limits
features.summary: Starting the week of January 12, 2026, group membership list endpoints such as Open Cloud ListGroupMemberships return 403 to non-members when a group hides its member list. Groups API rate limits tighten December 11, 2025. Audit logs gain TargetDisplayName.
replaces: Assuming group member list endpoints always succeed for any caller
Reading audit log TargetName as the target user's display name
features.guidance: When you call ListGroupMemberships (GET /cloud/v2/groups/{groupId}/memberships) with open_cloud_invoke, or call GET /v1/groups/{groupId}/users or /v1/groups/{groupId}/roles/{roleSetId}/users, handle 403 Forbidden. It applies from the week of January 12, 2026. Retry 429s with backoff, since limits tighten December 11, 2025. Use audit log TargetDisplayName for display names.

features.name: Luau New Type Solver
features.summary: Luau's New Type Solver is out of beta. It's on by default for nocheck and nonstrict scripts and gives better inference, a redesigned nonstrict mode, and type functions. Workspace.UseNewLuauTypeSolver turns it on or off, and Workspace.LuauTypeCheckMode sets the default mode.
replaces: New Type Solver Studio beta
Non-Strict by Default Studio beta
Adding --!nonstrict or --!strict to every script to change the default mode
Casting through any to reach a specific type
features.guidance: Assume the New Type Solver checks nocheck and nonstrict scripts, and strict scripts when Workspace.UseNewLuauTypeSolver is Enabled. Read both Workspace properties with inspect_instance. If a strict project needs the solver turned on or a different default mode, ask the user to set it in Workspace Properties under Scripting. Script directives still override LuauTypeCheckMode.

features.name: Aim Assist (AimAssistController module)
features.summary: The FPS and Laser Tag Studio templates now include aim assist. It's a reusable AimAssistController ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage that applies friction, tracking, and centering toward targets with a CollectionService tag, for gamepad and touch players.
replaces: Hand-written aim assist or controller aim-slowdown code in shooters
features.guidance: No MCP tool fetches the module, so ask the user to copy AimAssistController and its children from the FPS or Laser Tag template into ReplicatedStorage, then confirm it's there with search_game_tree. Tag targets with Instance:AddTag. On weapon equip, call setSubject(Workspace.CurrentCamera), addTargetTag, addPlayerTargets, setRange, setFieldOfView, setMethodStrength and enable().

features.name: ReflectionService engine API reflection
features.summary: ReflectionService lets Luau query the Engine API: classes with GetClass and GetClasses, plus properties, methods, and events with GetPropertiesOfClass, GetMethodsOfClass, and GetEventsOfClass. Use it to build API inspection and class-changing tools.
features.guidance: To find a class's properties, methods, or events, run ReflectionService:GetPropertiesOfClass, GetMethodsOfClass, or GetEventsOfClass with execute_luau, passing the class name, such as "Part". Results are filtered to the calling context's SecurityCapabilities. Pass { Security = SecurityCapabilities.new() } to get only APIs that every context can access.

features.name: Data Stores Batch Processor CLI
features.summary: Roblox's open-source Data Stores Batch Processor CLI runs your own Luau logic across many data stores or keys through Open Cloud. It runs outside live game servers, for bulk deletion and schema migrations such as moving off DataStore2.
replaces: Migrating or deleting old player data in game servers when players join
Keeping two data schemas supported in game code during a migration
Leaving stale DataStore2 or 'Berezaa Method' data in storage
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs the batch processor. For bulk data deletion or schema migration, suggest that the user download it from https://github.com/Roblox/data-stores-batch-processor-cli and run it from their own machine or server after reading the README. You can help write the custom Luau logic. To clear a whole data store, suggest the Open Cloud Data Store Deletion API instead.

features.name: HapticEffect Ended event
features.summary: HapticEffect.Ended fires when a HapticEffect has finished playing and stopped. You can then destroy the effect at the right time to save memory. The Platformer, Laser Tag/FPS, and Racing Studio templates now include haptics examples.
replaces: Destroying a HapticEffect after a guessed delay instead of when playback ends
features.guidance: For one-shot haptics, create a HapticEffect, set its Type (for example Enum.HapticEffectType.GameplayExplosion), call Play, and connect Ended to destroy the effect once playback finishes. For example haptics setups, suggest the user open the Platformer, Laser Tag/FPS, or Racing template from the Templates tab in Studio. No MCP tool opens templates.

features.name: Capture Upload API and RecommendationService
features.summary: Beta APIs for in-experience content sharing. CaptureService:UploadCaptureAsync lets players upload captures from their gallery as assets. RecommendationService ranks registered content, such as player videos, for each player.
replaces: Asking players to share captures outside the experience
Hand-built ranking of player content in DataStores
features.guidance: To upload, call PromptCaptureGalleryPermissionAsync(Enum.CaptureGalleryPermission.ReadAndUpload), then ReadCapturesFromGalleryAsync and page through the results, then wrap UploadCaptureAsync in pcall and check each result enum. On the server, register items with RecommendationService:RegisterItemAsync(player, request), and keep the metadata in your own DataStore. Both are in beta and work in experiences now.

features.name: GeometryService CSG, Fragment, and Sweep APIs
features.summary: GeometryService:UnionAsync, SubtractAsync, and IntersectAsync do CSG in published experiences and now accept watertight MeshParts. FragmentAsync and GenerateFragmentSites break parts into pieces, and SweepPartAsync sweeps a part along CFrames into one MeshPart for clean cuts.
replaces: BasePart:UnionAsync
BasePart:SubtractAsync
BasePart:IntersectAsync
Many separate SubtractAsync calls along a path to cut a part
Pre-splitting parts into pieces by hand for destruction
features.guidance: Use GeometryService CSG, not BasePart CSG methods. To break a part, pass GenerateFragmentSites(part) to FragmentAsync and parent each result's .Instance; for clean cuts, SubtractAsync the result of SweepPartAsync(tool, cframes). These work live; only Studio's CSG buttons on MeshParts (Solid Modeling on Meshes) and rbxNegated Negate (Updated Solid Modeling Buttons) are betas the user turns on in File > Beta Features.

features.name: Rewarded Video ads (AdService)
features.summary: Rewarded Video ads are now open to all ads-eligible creators (13+, 2FA, ID-verified, public experience with 2,000+ monthly visitors). Players choose to watch a video for a developer product reward. Use AdService:GetAdAvailabilityNowAsync and AdService:ShowRewardedVideoAdAsync.
features.guidance: On the client, pcall AdService:GetAdAvailabilityNowAsync(Enum.AdFormat.RewardedVideo) and show the ad button only if it's IsAvailable. On the server, pcall AdService:ShowRewardedVideoAdAsync(player, AdService:CreateAdRewardFromDevProductId(productId)) and grant the product in MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt. Ask the user to enable Rewarded Video Ads in Game Settings > Monetization.

features.name: Highlight limit raised to 255
features.summary: An experience's DataModel can now hold up to 255 Highlight instances, so you can outline or overlay many more objects at once without scripts that juggle a few Highlights. It's live in published experiences.
replaces: Scripting workarounds to stay under the old Highlight instance limit, such as reusing a small pool of Highlights
features.guidance: When many objects need an outline or overlay, such as collectibles or interactive items, give each its own Highlight, up to 255 per DataModel, rather than writing code to pool or reuse a few. Each highlighted object costs a draw call, and any Highlight on screen adds a post-processing cost, so use only as many as you need.

features.name: Avatar Makeup preview in Avatar Setup
features.summary: The Avatar Setup plugin can now preview Avatar Makeup, meaning Decals with WrapTextureTransfer, on an avatar. You can reorder layers, assign Face, Lips, or Eyes regions, try other skin tones, and play animations. It needs the Avatar Makeup Studio beta.
replaces: Assembling and previewing makeup looks by hand in the Explorer
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs Avatar Setup, so ask the user to turn on Avatar Makeup in File > Beta Features, open Avatar > Setup, pick the avatar, select makeup Decals with WrapTextureTransfer, click +, and set each to Face, Lips, or Eyes. You can parent eyebrow and eyelash MeshParts under the avatar model with execute_luau first. Makeup doesn't work in published experiences yet.

features.name: Dynamic server CPU scaling by player count
features.summary: Each server's CPU limit now has a higher baseline plus a fixed amount for each connected player, in place of a fixed limit based on Max Players. It rolled out to all experiences automatically from November 10 to 12, 2025. There is no API for it.
replaces: Fixed server CPU limit based on Max Players
features.guidance: Don't plan server CPU budgets around Max Players or a fixed limit. Each server's limit follows the players connected to that server, not the total across all servers. Servers with few players, including single-player ones, get more CPU than before. The CPU isn't faster, so check any system that scales its work with player count. For optimization tips, fetch the performance-optimization docs with http_get.

features.name: Experience event lookup and RSVP prompts
features.summary: SocialService:GetUpcomingExperienceEventsAsync lists the experience's upcoming events, soonest first. GetExperienceEventAsync gets one event's details by ID, so RSVP prompts don't need hardcoded IDs. GetEventRsvpStatusAsync and PromptRsvpToEventAsync check and prompt RSVPs.
replaces: Hardcoded event IDs passed to SocialService:PromptRsvpToEventAsync
features.guidance: Don't hardcode event IDs: call SocialService:GetUpcomingExperienceEventsAsync (event dictionaries, soonest first) or GetExperienceEventAsync, then pass the event's ID as a string to PromptRsvpToEventAsync. Wrap these calls in pcall, call the RSVP methods from client code, and update RSVP UI from the Enum.RsvpStatus PromptRsvpToEventAsync returns. All work in published experiences.

features.name: PlayerRemoving exitReason (PlayerExitReason)
features.summary: Players.PlayerRemoving now passes an optional second parameter, exitReason, a PlayerExitReason enum (Unknown, PlatformKick, CreatorKick) that tells server scripts why a player left the experience.
replaces: Setting a flag or attribute by hand before Player:Kick to tell kicks apart from other exits in PlayerRemoving
features.guidance: In server scripts, connect Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player, exitReason) ... end) and compare exitReason to Enum.PlayerExitReason.CreatorKick or Enum.PlayerExitReason.PlatformKick. Read it only on the server. On the client it's always Enum.PlayerExitReason.Unknown. Treat Unknown as 'reason not known', not as a confirmed voluntary leave.

features.name: Open Cloud Assets API: rbxm, animation, mesh uploads
features.summary: The Open Cloud Assets API now uploads .rbxm/.rbxmx models, .rbxm/.rbxmx animations, and Roblox-format meshes. The cookie-based legacy upload endpoints on data.roblox.com were deprecated about a week after March 2, 2026. Use the Assets API for these uploads.
replaces: https://data.roblox.com/Data/Upload.ashx
https://data.roblox.com/ide/publish/UploadNewMesh
https://data.roblox.com/ide/publish/UploadNewAnimation
User-cookie-authenticated asset uploads
Re-uploading animations to share them across accounts
features.guidance: To upload .rbxm/.rbxmx models or animations, Roblox-format meshes, or FBX/glTF models, call the Open Cloud Assets API (assets/v1) with open_cloud_invoke. Never use the data.roblox.com upload endpoints. To let other users, groups, or experiences use an animation, suggest Animation Sharing rather than re-uploading it, and ask the user to run the 3D Importer when import settings need tuning.

features.name: User Provided Default Instances
features.summary: Studio users can save a selected instance as the default for its class with Save as Default and undo that with Reset Default. Insert Object and Insert Part then use the saved properties, tags, and attributes. Instance.new isn't affected.
replaces: Changing the same properties by hand on every part or object inserted in Studio
Using the ribbon Color and Material pickers to set Insert Part's color and material
features.guidance: No MCP tool sets these defaults, and they don't affect Instance.new or execute_luau. When a user keeps fixing the same properties on objects they insert, suggest they select one and choose Edit > Save as Default in the system menu. In code, set properties yourself, for example with a helper that configures Instance.new results.

features.name: HttpService WebStreamClient (SSE and WebSockets)
features.summary: HttpService:CreateWebStreamClient opens a live connection from a Studio plugin to an external server. It can use Server-Sent Events or two-way WebSockets, which send with WebStreamClient:Send. Use it for live syncing, debugging, and language servers. It works in Studio only.
replaces: Long-polling an external server with HttpService requests from a Studio plugin
features.guidance: In plugins, call HttpService:CreateWebStreamClient with Enum.WebStreamClientType.SSE for one-way streams or Enum.WebStreamClientType.WebSocket for two-way traffic, then connect MessageReceived and Closed and send with WebStreamClient:Send on WebSockets. Live experiences block these calls, so remove them before publishing. Secrets Stores don't work with plugins, so keep secrets out of shared code.

features.name: ParticleEmitter custom flipbook layouts
features.summary: Enum.ParticleFlipbookLayout.Custom, together with ParticleEmitter.FlipbookSizeX and FlipbookSizeY, lets particle flipbooks use grids that aren't square, from 1 to 64 columns and rows. Textures no longer have to be square, so sprite sheets don't need empty padding.
replaces: Padding sprite sheets with empty frames or space to fit a square Grid2x2, Grid4x4, or Grid8x8 layout
Making flipbook textures square only to meet the flipbook requirement
features.guidance: For a sprite sheet whose grid isn't square, set the ParticleEmitter's FlipbookLayout to Enum.ParticleFlipbookLayout.Custom. Then set FlipbookSizeX to the number of columns and FlipbookSizeY to the number of rows, each from 1 to 64. Do this with execute_luau or in a script. The announcement doesn't say if this client beta works in published experiences, so check it in a playtest and tell the user it's a beta.

features.name: Stats.MemoryTrackingEnabled
features.summary: Stats.MemoryTrackingEnabled tells you whether engine memory tracking is on for this session. On most Android devices it's now off, so GetMemoryUsageMbAllCategories, GetMemoryUsageMbForTag and GetTotalMemoryUsageMb return 0 there.
replaces: Calling Stats memory APIs without checking whether tracking is on
Treating a 0 from Stats memory APIs as real memory usage
features.guidance: Before calling GetMemoryUsageMbAllCategories, GetMemoryUsageMbForTag or GetTotalMemoryUsageMb, check game:GetService("Stats").MemoryTrackingEnabled. If it's false, skip the memory readings in telemetry or logic instead of recording or acting on the 0s. The value stays the same for the whole session, so you can read it once and cache it.

features.name: HumanoidDescription asset type verification default
features.summary: Starting 2025-10-27, the assetTypeVerification argument of Humanoid:ApplyDescription and Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromDescription defaults to Enum.AssetTypeVerification.Always, not ClientOnly. The server now checks the type of every asset loaded onto a humanoid.
replaces: Relying on the old ClientOnly default to load custom or non-avatar assets through HumanoidDescription
features.guidance: Since 2025-10-27 these calls default to Enum.AssetTypeVerification.Always, which blocks asset types that aren't avatar assets. Keep the default for avatar catalog items. Pass Enum.AssetTypeVerification.ClientOnly only for trusted custom or non-avatar assets that you made or checked, and limit user choices to a whitelist. Use script_grep to find these calls.

features.name: Proximity Prompt Indicators
features.summary: ProximityPrompt.MaxIndicatorDistance shows a built-in indicator for prompts that are in range but not yet active, or hidden by ProximityPromptService.MaxPromptsVisible or exclusivity. Use it to guide players to things they can interact with without cluttering the screen.
replaces: Hand-built BillboardGui markers that point players to distant ProximityPrompts
Setting many prompts to AlwaysShow so players can see every nearby interactable
features.guidance: To show distant interactables, set MaxIndicatorDistance higher than MaxActivationDistance on the ProximityPrompt instead of building your own BillboardGui markers. Set ProximityPromptService.MaxIndicatorsVisible (default 16, max 64) if you need more indicators. For custom indicator visuals, connect to ProximityPrompt.IndicatorShown/IndicatorHidden or the matching ProximityPromptService events.

features.name: Share Link API (PromptLinkSharing)
features.summary: SocialService:PromptLinkSharing creates a short share link with LaunchData for deep linking, a custom preview title and description, and an expiry with a fallback link. It then opens the player's share sheet and returns an Enum.PromptLinkSharingResult.
replaces: Sharing the plain experience join link, which can't carry LaunchData or a custom preview
features.guidance: In a server Script, wrap SocialService:PromptLinkSharingAsync(player, options) in pcall. Options are LaunchData (a JSON string from HttpService:JSONEncode), PreviewTitle, PreviewDescription, ExpirationSeconds and FallbackLinkId. Check that the result is Enum.PromptLinkSharingResult.Success. On join, read player:GetJoinData().LaunchData to send the player to the right place or give the reward.

features.name: Advanced Video API (VideoPlayer and VideoDisplay)
features.summary: A Studio beta that adds VideoPlayer, which holds a video and controls playback, and VideoDisplay, which shows it on a GUI. You connect them with Wires. Use it to play one video in sync on many surfaces, send its audio through AudioEmitters and effects, and change speed and appearance.
replaces: Several VideoFrames playing the same video on different surfaces
Restarting playback to move a video from one surface to another
features.guidance: Ask the user to turn on New Video API in File > Beta Features and restart Studio. It doesn't work in published experiences yet. Wire one VideoPlayer to VideoDisplays under SurfaceGuis, ScreenGuis, or BillboardGuis, and to an AudioEmitter for 3D audio, which needs an AudioListener. Call VideoPlayer:LoadAsync on the client to preload.

features.name: Security Tactics and Cheat Mitigation guide
features.summary: A rewritten Security Tactics and Cheat Mitigation guide covers how to secure a game against common attacks: Never Trust the Client, defensive game design that makes exploits less valuable, securing universe structure, keeping server logic confidential, and decoy systems that detect exploiters.
features.guidance: Before you write gameplay or networking code that takes client input, fetch the guide with http_get and follow it. Treat whatever the client sends as untrusted, keep confidential server logic away from clients, and design systems so exploits are worth less. Use script_grep and script_read to check existing scripts against these principles.

features.name: glTF Export and Quick 3D Import
features.summary: Studio exports selected Workspace items or a whole place to one .gltf file with embedded textures. It keeps hierarchy, PBR textures, skinning, rigs, vertex colors, and dynamic heads. Alt+M or Option+M Quick Import brings in one 3D file using default settings.
replaces: OBJ export for moving Roblox content into external 3D applications
Going through the full Import 3D dialog to import a single 3D file with default settings
features.guidance: No MCP tool exports or imports 3D files. To edit Roblox content in Blender or Maya, ask the user to put it in a Folder or Model in Workspace, then use Explorer > Save / Export > Export as glTF or File > Export as glTF. To bring in one 3D file, ask them to press Alt+M (Option+M on Mac) for Quick Import, which uses the Studio Default settings.

features.name: UIStroke scaled thickness, border position, and offset
features.summary: UIStroke.StrokeSizingMode lets Thickness scale with the parent's shortest axis. UIStroke.BorderStrokePosition draws strokes on the inside, center, or outside of a border, and UIStroke.BorderOffset shifts them further. One GuiObject can now have several border strokes.
replaces: Scripts that recompute UIStroke.Thickness from the parent's AbsoluteSize
Invisible wrapper Frame instances for layered or inset stroke effects
features.guidance: To scale a stroke with its parent, set StrokeSizingMode to Enum.StrokeSizingMode.ScaledSize and set Thickness between 0 and 1 as a fraction of the parent's shortest axis. Don't resize it from a script. For inset or layered outlines, parent several border UIStrokes to one GuiObject, each with its own BorderStrokePosition, BorderOffset (UDim), and a distinct ZIndex. Don't use wrapper Frames.

features.name: Light Range limit raised to 120
features.summary: The maximum Range for PointLight, SpotLight, and SurfaceLight is now 120 studs instead of 60, so fewer lights can cover large spaces. Scripted Range values above 60 are no longer clamped to 60, so they now render with a larger range.
replaces: Using several 60-range lights to cover one large area
features.guidance: Set PointLight.Range, SpotLight.Range, or SurfaceLight.Range up to 120 to light large areas with fewer lights. Values above 120 are clamped to 120. Scripts that set Range above 60 now light a larger area, so use script_grep for ".Range" and lower any values the user wants to stay at 60.

features.name: TextGenerator LLM text generation
features.summary: The TextGenerator class runs open-source LLMs at runtime through TextGenerator:GenerateTextAsync to build NPCs that reply in context, guided by a SystemPrompt. It's now open to experiences of any content maturity rating and replaces the Open Cloud Text Generation API.
replaces: Open Cloud Text Generation API
Calling external LLM services through HttpService
features.guidance: Create a TextGenerator, set SystemPrompt, and call GenerateTextAsync({UserPrompt = text}) inside pcall, then read response.GeneratedText. Move off the Open Cloud Text Generation API, which is being deprecated over the 90 days after 2025-09-22. The beta works in published experiences of any maturity rating, but ask the user to retake the maturity questionnaire if the game centers on AI chat.

features.name: Data Store deletion
features.summary: The Open Cloud DeleteDataStore API, in public beta, deletes a whole Data Store after a 30-day cooldown, and UndeleteDataStore cancels the deletion. Reads and writes to the store fail as soon as deletion is scheduled.
replaces: Removing every key of a Data Store one by one to clear it
features.guidance: Before deleting, use script_grep to find DataStoreService:GetDataStore calls that use the store's name. Then call DeleteDataStore through open_cloud_invoke. These are public beta Open Cloud APIs that act on live data. Reads and writes fail at once in published experiences too, so if errors say 'The data store is deleted', call UndeleteDataStore within 30 days.

features.name: AssetService:LoadAssetAsync
features.summary: AssetService:LoadAssetAsync loads any asset that contains Instances, such as Models, Decals, or Animations, and returns a sandboxed Model with scripts disabled. With Allow Loading Third Party Assets on, it loads third-party Free Models. It's the planned replacement for InsertService:LoadAsset.
replaces: InsertService:LoadAsset
features.guidance: In new code, load assets with AssetService:LoadAssetAsync(assetId) instead of InsertService:LoadAsset. Scripts in the returned Model don't run unless you grant Capabilities to it. To load Free Models you don't own, ask the user to turn on Game Settings > Security > Allow Loading Third Party Assets. The agent can't change that setting, and it's off by default.

features.name: Photo-to-Avatar generation APIs
features.summary: Alpha AvatarCreationService APIs turn a player's live selfie into a rigged, FACS-enabled avatar. Start with RequestAvatarGenerationSessionAsync, make a 2D preview, then call GenerateAvatarAsync. Players can buy and save the result with PromptCreateAvatarAsync.
features.guidance: On the server, call RequestAvatarGenerationSessionAsync, then GenerateAvatar2DPreviewAsync (SessionId, the client's PromptSelectAvatarGenerationImageAsync fileId, optional prompt), then GenerateAvatarAsync (SessionId, PreviewId). Load results on the client with LoadAvatar2DPreviewAsync and LoadGeneratedAvatarAsync. The alpha works in published experiences on iOS and Android only.

features.name: Find/Replace All widget
features.summary: Studio's Find/Replace All widget was rebuilt in Luau to search, step through, and replace thousands of matches across all scripts. It adds Replace All with a confirmation prompt, regex validation, arrow-key navigation of results, and a maximum-results setting.
replaces: Editing many scripts one at a time to rename or replace text across a place
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs Find/Replace All. For small edits, use script_grep (up to 50 matches) with script_read and multi_edit. For replacements across many scripts, suggest the user open the widget with Ctrl+Shift+F (Cmd+Shift+F on Mac), or Ctrl+Shift+H (Cmd+Shift+H) to open the Replace panel, and then run Replace All.

features.name: Studio Early Access Programs
features.summary: Early Access Programs let selected creators opt into and out of custom experimental Studio builds, earlier than a Studio Beta. They pick a program from the Early Access dropdown on the Settings page after signing up through a DevForum announcement.
replaces: Waiting for Roblox staff to add an account to, or remove it from, a Studio test channel
features.guidance: No MCP tool joins or leaves a program. Ask the user to sign up through the program's DevForum link, then pick it in the Early Access dropdown on the Settings page ('No Program Selected' to leave) and restart Studio. Experiences that use Early Access features can't be published, and their APIs will likely change, so don't rely on them in production code.

features.name: AudioPlayer volume doubled to match Sound
features.summary: AudioPlayer used to play at 50% of its expected volume. It now plays twice as loud and matches Sound at the same AudioPlayer.Volume. The SoundService.AudioPlayerVolumeFix opt-out has been removed, so this can't be turned off.
replaces: SoundService.AudioPlayerVolumeFix (temporary opt-out, removed)
Raising AudioPlayer.Volume to make up for the old 50% playback level
features.guidance: Set AudioPlayer.Volume to the same value you'd give a Sound. Don't use SoundService.AudioPlayerVolumeFix, which no longer exists. If the user says their AudioPlayer volumes were tuned before the change, find them with search_game_tree (instance type AudioPlayer) and script_grep for "AudioPlayer", then halve Volume with execute_luau or multi_edit and playtest.

features.name: MicroProfiler Network Plugin
features.summary: The MicroProfiler now has a Network Plugin that shows how much data was sent and received in captured frames. It adds a verbosity menu and an events window that breaks down individual network events, such as asset deliveries with their asset IDs. Use it to find causes of latency and slow loading.
replaces: Guessing at network usage and latency causes when the MicroProfiler only showed CPU and memory
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs the MicroProfiler. When a user reports heavy network use, latency, or slow asset loading, suggest the Network Plugin: ask them to open the MicroProfiler, capture frames, and check the traffic graphs and events window to see which assets or events caused spikes. You can start a playtest with start_stop_play and read the docs with http_get.

features.name: Animation asset permissions
features.summary: Animation assets are 'Restricted' like Audio and Video, and can be shared with connections, groups, and experiences from the Animation's Permissions page in Creator Hub. Once an experience has permission, every player can load it there and every collaborator can load it in Studio playtests.
replaces: Re-uploading or transferring Animations to the experience owner's account or group
Re-uploading Animations and updating references after an experience ownership transfer
Giving group collaborators the legacy 'Create and edit community experiences' permission so Animations load in Studio
Re-uploading an Animation so a connection or group can use it
features.guidance: If an Animation fails to load, run start_stop_play and check get_console_output; the experience gets permission automatically when the user can share the Animation. Otherwise ask the user to grant the experience on the Animation's Creator Hub Permissions page, or ask its owner to share it with them or their group under Collaborators. Animations can't be set to Open Use.

features.name: In-experience Avatar Switcher
features.summary: Players can switch avatars from the in-experience menu. The change applies when they respawn, so it depends on respawn being enabled. Game code can hide the Switch Avatar option with StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.AvatarSwitcher, false).
replaces: StarterGui:SetCore("ResetButtonCallback", false) to block avatar switching
features.guidance: To turn the switcher off, call StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.AvatarSwitcher, false) from a client script such as a LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts. Don't disable respawn just to block avatar switching. To allow switching, keep respawn on, at least in lobbies. A custom ResetButtonCallback BindableEvent runs when a player respawns from the switcher, so handle it there.

features.name: LoadAsset for shared Model and MeshPart assets
features.summary: InsertService:LoadAsset can now load Model and MeshPart assets that a Connection or group shared with you, not only ones you uploaded. The experience needs permission for each asset in Creator Hub.
features.guidance: To load a collaborator's shared Model or MeshPart at runtime, call InsertService:LoadAsset(assetId). First ask the user to give the experience permission for that asset in Creator Hub > Experience Permissions > Assets. This also covers the Restricted assets it references. require() on shared assets hasn't changed: the module must be listed on the store and have a MainModule.

features.name: ROG Xbox Ally handhelds and Studio handheld emulator
features.summary: Roblox runs on ROG Xbox Ally and ROG Xbox Ally X handhelds, which count as Console devices along with older handhelds like the ROG Ally. Studio now has a Generic Handheld HD emulator with a Generic Handheld virtual controller for testing them.
features.guidance: These handhelds count as Console, so design for gamepad input and small screens. No MCP tool runs the emulator or publishes to Console: ask the user to pick Generic Handheld HD under Console in Test > Device (Test > Device Emulator in next-gen Studio) with the Generic Handheld controller, then publish to Console. The skill tool's device simulation material may help.

features.name: ViewportDisplaySize (Small/Medium/Large screens)
features.summary: GuiService.ViewportDisplaySize is a read-only property that sorts the physical size of the player's viewport into Enum.DisplaySize Small, Medium, or Large. Use it to adapt UI layout across devices instead of guessing screen size from resolution or input type.
replaces: Guessing display size from Camera.ViewportSize resolution breakpoints
Using UserInputService.TouchEnabled, GamepadEnabled, or KeyboardEnabled to infer screen size for UI layout
features.guidance: In a LocalScript, branch UI layout on GuiService.ViewportDisplaySize (Small is most phones and tablets, Medium is most laptops and monitors, Large is most TVs) and rerun it from GuiService:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportDisplaySize"). Use UserInputService.PreferredInput for input-specific UI instead of TouchEnabled, GamepadEnabled, or KeyboardEnabled. Don't use it to pick rendering quality.

features.name: Improved gamepad Directional UI Selection
features.summary: Default gamepad Directional UI Selection now follows the analog thumbstick angle, skips fully covered elements, keeps D-pad moves inside the current panel, starts on the highest-ZIndex element, and selects with R2. GuiBase2d.SelectionGroup and SelectionBehavior overrides still take precedence.
replaces: Hand-written navigation overrides that only fixed diagonal moves, selection of covered elements, or D-pad moves leaving a panel
features.guidance: Rely on default Directional UI Selection for gamepad UI. Set GuiBase2d.SelectionGroup or SelectionBehaviorUp/Down/Left/Right only where you need custom navigation, because these override the defaults. No MCP tool sends gamepad input, so ask the user to test with a gamepad: thumbstick, D-pad, and R2.

features.name: Replicated child order only guaranteed for Gui objects
features.summary: Replication in experiences and Team Create now keeps child order only for GuiBase2d objects and Folders inside a GuiBase hierarchy. For other instances, the order of Instance:GetChildren can change, and Instance.ChildAdded can fire for a child in the middle of the list.
replaces: Relying on Instance:GetChildren order for non-Gui instances
Assuming the child passed to ChildAdded is last in the child list
features.guidance: Outside Gui hierarchies, don't write code that depends on Instance:GetChildren order, such as indexing GetChildren()[1]. Sort the children yourself, for example by Name or an attribute. In ChildAdded handlers, don't assume the new child is at the end of the list. Use script_grep to find GetChildren()[ and check that kind of code.

features.name: Multiple Replication Foci (streaming)
features.summary: With StreamingEnabled, Player:AddReplicationFocus(part) streams the area around a BasePart to a player, in addition to their character or ReplicationFocus. Areas stay loaded and client physics keeps running there. Use it for home bases, hubs, spectating, and scopes.
replaces: Calling Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync over and over to keep a distant area streamed in
Setting very large Workspace.StreamingMinRadius or StreamingTargetRadius values to keep far-away areas loaded
features.guidance: From a server Script, call player:AddReplicationFocus(part) for each player who needs the area, passing a BasePart, and call RemoveReplicationFocus when they no longer need it. Each focus uses the Workspace min and target radii, and only the part's position counts. Add as few foci as you can, especially moving ones, because each one adds server and client cost.

features.name: Texture Generator Style Control and Prompt Weighting
features.summary: The Texture Generator Studio beta now takes an uploaded style image with a strength slider (Style Control). It also lets you add emphasis in prompts with + and -, or with numeric weights like (robotic)1.5 (Prompt Weighting).
replaces: Rewording Texture Generator prompts over and over to get the right style, colors, or emphasis
features.guidance: No MCP tool runs Texture Generator, so suggest it when the user wants a texture with a set style. Ask them to turn on Texture Generator in File > Beta Features, upload a style image they have rights to, set its strength, and weight prompt terms, such as 'a futuristic pirate++ backpack' or '(futuristic)--'. For new textured meshes or material variants, call generate_mesh or generate_material.

features.name: Cube 3D mesh generation SuggestedSize
features.summary: An updated Cube 3D model gives GenerationService:GenerateMeshAsync better meshes and textures. It adds an optional SuggestedSize Vector3 that sets the generated mesh's proportions, and the rate limit goes from 5 to 30 generations per minute per experience.
replaces: Rescaling a generated mesh after generation to fit a space
features.guidance: In experiences, ask the user to turn on the EditableMesh/EditableImage APIs in File > Game Settings > Security. Then pass a Vector3 as the optional SuggestedSize to GenerationService:GenerateMeshAsync so the model builds the shape at those proportions, and check the GenerationService docs for the exact argument shape. This beta works in published experiences. In Studio, call the generate_mesh MCP tool instead of Assistant's /generate.

features.name: Avatar Settings
features.summary: Avatar Settings is a Studio window (File > Avatar Settings, or the Avatar tab) for setting player avatar height and proportions, a single box collider, clothing and accessory limits, and animation packs, with presets such as Consistent Gameplay.
replaces: Custom scripts that rescale player avatars to a consistent height
Custom scripts that remove or replace oversized clothing and accessories
Custom scripts that give avatars a uniform hitbox or collider
features.guidance: No MCP tool opens Avatar Settings; ask the user to set avatar height, Single Collider, clothing limits, and animation packs in File > Avatar Settings instead of scripting avatar scaling. With Single Collider, don't expect HumanoidRootPart or torso parts to collide, and allow an invisible CollisionPart under HumanoidRootPart. With Custom Scale, use the configured height, not a measured one.

features.name: Video Captures API
features.summary: CaptureService:StartVideoCaptureAsync and CaptureService:StopVideoCapture record video clips of up to 30 seconds at key gameplay moments. The result is a temporary VideoCapture that you can prompt the user to save with PromptSaveCapturesToGallery.
features.guidance: Call CaptureService:StartVideoCaptureAsync(onCaptureReady, {}) at a key moment and StopVideoCapture() to end it; recording stops itself at 30 seconds. In onCaptureReady, on Enum.VideoCaptureResult.Success or TimeLimitReached, pass the VideoCapture to PromptSaveCapturesToGallery. It's rolling out gradually to users, so if the call doesn't return Enum.VideoCaptureStartedResult.Success, show the player a message.

features.name: SavePlaceAsync for Studio-created places
