features.summary: AssetService:SavePlaceAsync can now save places created in Studio or Creator Hub, not only places made with CreatePlaceAsync. Turn on the place's 'Allow place to be updated using Save Place API' permission first so game code can save player changes.
replaces: Creating places with AssetService:CreatePlaceAsync only so that SavePlaceAsync can save them
features.guidance: To call AssetService:SavePlaceAsync on a place made in Studio or Creator Hub, ask the user to turn on 'Allow place to be updated using Save Place API' in that place's Permissions on Creator Hub. Without it, the save fails. Places made with CreatePlaceAsync don't need it. To save the place that's open in Studio, call save_place instead.

features.name: Memory Stores Extended Services and higher limits
features.summary: MemoryStoreService default limits rose 20%, to 1000 + (CCU x 120) request units and 64KB + (D8PCU x 1.2KB) storage. Experiences that need more request units or storage can now buy them through Extended Services.
replaces: Designing Memory Store usage to fit the old default limits
features.guidance: Plan Memory Store code around the defaults: 1000 + (CCU x 120) request units and 64KB + (D8PCU x 1.2KB) storage, where D8PCU is peak concurrent users over 8 days. If usage might go over these, ask the user to check the Memory Stores Observability Dashboard. To go higher, they must set up an Extended Services account and buy more on the experience's Extended Services page in Creator Hub.

features.name: Sky.SkyboxOrientation skybox rotation
features.summary: Sky.SkyboxOrientation is a Vector3 property that rotates a Sky's skybox textures, in degrees, at low performance cost and no memory cost. It replicates and can be animated from scripts to spin, tilt, or flip the sky.
features.guidance: Set Sky.SkyboxOrientation on the Sky under Lighting to a Vector3 of angles in degrees. Rotation applies Y first, then X, then Z, so animate Y for a spin, for example in RunService.Heartbeat with % 360, and use X and Z for a fixed tilt.

features.name: Detached Attachments (Attachments without a BasePart)
features.summary: An Attachment no longer needs a BasePart ancestor. You can parent it to Workspace, a Folder, a Model, or the Camera. Its CFrame is relative to its nearest PVInstance or Attachment ancestor, or to world space if it has neither. It's meant for VFX, SFX, and positioning points.
replaces: Invisible, anchored, non-collidable parts that exist only to hold an Attachment
Scripts that move an Attachment's holder part every frame to follow a Model or the Camera
features.guidance: To place particles, sounds, or other effects, parent the Attachment directly to a Model, Folder, the Camera, or Workspace. Don't create a holder part for it. Constraints only work when both Attachments have a BasePart ancestor, because massless detached Attachments turn them off. When attaching to a large Model, set Model.PrimaryPart so Attachment.CFrame doesn't have to scan every part to find the pivot.

features.name: UserInputService.PreferredInput
features.summary: UserInputService.PreferredInput reports the player's main input type as Enum.PreferredInput: KeyboardAndMouse, Gamepad, or Touch. Use it for button prompts, input labels, and UI layouts across platforms. TouchEnabled now correctly returns true on any device with a touch surface.
replaces: Guessing the input type from UserInputService.KeyboardEnabled, MouseEnabled, TouchEnabled, and GamepadEnabled
Tracking UserInputService.LastInputTypeChanged by hand to switch UI modes
Using UserInputService.TouchEnabled to decide whether to show mobile UI
features.guidance: To pick prompts, hotkey labels, or touch versus keyboard UI, read UserInputService.PreferredInput, compare it to Enum.PreferredInput items, and update on UserInputService:GetPropertyChangedSignal("PreferredInput"). Don't show mobile UI just because TouchEnabled is true, since hybrid Windows devices now report true. Keep TouchEnabled and LastInputType for checking whether an input is available.

features.name: EditableMesh bones, skinning, and FACS
features.summary: EditableMesh can now read and edit a mesh's embedded bones (AddBone, SetBoneCFrame), vertex skinning (SetVertexBones, SetVertexBoneWeights), and FACS poses (SetFacsPose) at runtime. Use it to rig, skin, and animate meshes procedurally, including R15 avatars built from scratch.
replaces: Rigging and skinning meshes in an external tool such as Blender and re-importing them to change bones or weights
features.guidance: Build a skeleton with EditableMesh:AddBone and SetBoneCFrame, skin vertices by calling SetVertexBones before SetVertexBoneWeights, and set facial poses with SetFacsPose for Enum.FacsActionUnit values. Mesh bones bind to Bone instances under the MeshPart by name, so give them matching names. It works in published experiences, and no Studio beta needs to be turned on.

features.name: MemoryStore sorted map and queue GetSize
features.summary: MemoryStoreSortedMap:GetSizeAsync and MemoryStoreQueue:GetSizeAsync return the number of items in a memory store sorted map or queue. MemoryStoreHashMap doesn't have this method.
replaces: Paging through a sorted map or queue to count its items
Keeping a separate item counter next to a sorted map or queue
features.guidance: To get the number of items in a memory store sorted map or queue, call GetSizeAsync on it. Don't page through it or keep your own counter. This is a public beta, and the announcement doesn't say whether it needs a beta setting or works in published experiences, so check with the user before you rely on it in a live game. Hash maps have no size method.

features.name: Party API and Party Simulator
features.summary: Player.PartyId, SocialService:GetPlayersByPartyId, and SocialService:GetPartyAsync tell you which players joined together through Roblox's Party feature. The Party Simulator plugin, in beta, lets you test this logic in Studio Server & Clients playtests.
replaces: Guessing groups from friend lists or join timing to keep parties together
Publishing and coordinating multiple devices and accounts to test party logic
features.guidance: Read Player.PartyId on the server only (empty if not in a party), group same-server members with SocialService:GetPlayersByPartyId, and pcall SocialService:GetPartyAsync for a non-empty PartyId. No MCP tool runs the beta Party Simulator; ask the user to enable it in File > Beta Features and assign test users to parties in a Server & Clients playtest. It simulates parties in Studio only.

features.name: Legacy BodyMovers
features.summary: BodyVelocity, BodyPosition, BodyGyro, BodyForce, BodyAngularVelocity, and BodyThrust are deprecated in favor of mover constraints.
features.guidance: Do not use BodyMovers. Use LinearVelocity, AlignPosition, AlignOrientation, VectorForce, or AngularVelocity instead.
